## DEV-3 — Webhooks Management

**ID:** DEV-3  
**Persona:** Developer, System Integrator  
**Preconditions:** User has developer access enabled, authenticated  
**Triggers:** Navigate to developer/webhooks, Set up event notifications  

### Primary Screens

**Web:**
- `(dashboard)/developer/webhooks/page.tsx` — Webhooks list
- `(dashboard)/developer/webhooks/new/page.tsx` — Create webhook
- `(dashboard)/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/page.tsx` — Webhook detail
- `(dashboard)/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/deliveries/page.tsx` — Delivery history
- `(dashboard)/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/deliveries/[deliveryId]/page.tsx` — Delivery detail
- `(dashboard)/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/retry-config/page.tsx` — Retry configuration
- `(dashboard)/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/security/page.tsx` — Security settings
- `(dashboard)/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/transform/page.tsx` — Payload transformation
- `(dashboard)/developer/webhooks/batch-retry/page.tsx` — Batch retry operations
- `(dashboard)/developer/webhooks/compare/page.tsx` — Compare webhooks

**Mobile:**
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/developer/webhooks/index.tsx` — Webhooks list
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/developer/webhooks/create/index.tsx` — Create webhook
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/index.tsx` — Webhook detail
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/deliveries/index.tsx` — Deliveries
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/deliveries/[deliveryId]/index.tsx` — Delivery detail
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/security/index.tsx` — Security
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/developer/webhooks/[webhookId]/transform/index.tsx` — Transform

#### System Touchpoints

**Backend:** users-be (webhook domain), communications-be (webhook delivery)  
**APIs:**
- GET /v1/developer/webhooks
- POST /v1/developer/webhooks
- GET /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}
- PUT /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}
- DELETE /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}
- POST /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}/test
- GET /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries
- GET /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}
- POST /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/retry
- POST /v1/developer/webhooks/batch-retry
- GET /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}/retry-config
- PUT /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}/retry-config
- GET /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}/security
- PUT /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}/security
- GET /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}/transform
- PUT /v1/developer/webhooks/{webhook_id}/transform

**Events Published:**
- webhook.subscribed.v1
- webhook.unsubscribed.v1
- webhook.updated.v1
- webhook.test_sent.v1
- webhook.delivered.v1
- webhook.failed.v1
- webhook.retried.v1

**Events Delivered (Examples):**
- user.created.v1
- user.updated.v1
- job.created.v1
- job.updated.v1
- proposal.submitted.v1
- contract.signed.v1
- payment.completed.v1
- message.sent.v1
- (Any event from the platform's event catalog)

#### Flow Steps

#### A) Create Webhook

1. User navigates to developer/webhooks
2. Clicks "Create Webhook" button
3. Fills in form:
   - Webhook URL (required, must be HTTPS)
   - Description (optional, max 500 chars)
   - Event subscriptions (multi-select):
     - Groups: User Events, Job Events, Proposal Events, Contract Events, Payment Events, etc.
     - Specific events within each group (checkbox list)
     - "Select All" option per group
   - Secret (auto-generate or custom):
     - Auto-generate: secure random 64-char string
     - Custom: user provides (min 32 chars)
   - Active status toggle (default: ON)
   - Advanced settings (expandable):
     - Content type: application/json (default) or application/x-www-form-urlencoded
     - Custom headers (key-value pairs)
     - SSL verification: ON (default) or OFF (for testing only)
4. Clicks "Create Webhook"
5. Backend validates:
   - URL is HTTPS (except localhost)
   - URL is reachable (optional ping test)
   - At least one event selected
   - Secret meets minimum length
6. Backend creates webhook
7. Success page displays:
   - Webhook ID
   - Webhook URL (with copy)
   - Secret (with copy) - shown only once with warning
   - Subscribed events list
   - "Test Webhook" button
8. Send email: "Webhook created: {URL}. Keep your secret secure."
9. User can click "Test Webhook" to send test event

#### B) View Webhooks List

1. User navigates to developer/webhooks
2. System displays webhooks in card/table layout:
   - Webhook URL (truncated with tooltip on hover)
   - Status badge (active/inactive/error)
   - Event subscriptions count (e.g., "12 events")
   - Recent delivery stats:
     - Success rate (last 7 days): {percentage}
     - Total deliveries: {count}
     - Failed deliveries: {count}
   - Last delivery timestamp
   - Quick actions: View, Edit, Test, Delete
3. Features:
   - Search by URL or description
   - Filter by: status, event type
   - Sort by: created date, last delivery, success rate
   - Bulk actions: Activate/deactivate selected
4. Empty state:
   - Illustration + message
   - "Create Your First Webhook" CTA
   - Link to webhook documentation

#### C) View Webhook Detail

1. User clicks on webhook from list
2. System displays webhook details:
   - Overview section:
     - Webhook URL (with copy)
     - Description
     - Status (active/inactive)
     - Created date, last modified
     - Toggle active/inactive
   - Subscribed Events section:
     - List of all subscribed events (grouped by category)
     - Add/remove events
   - Statistics section (last 7 days):
     - Total deliveries: {count}
     - Successful: {count} ({percentage}%)
     - Failed: {count} ({percentage}%)
     - Average response time: {ms}
     - Fastest delivery: {ms}
     - Slowest delivery: {ms}
   - Recent Deliveries section:
     - Last 10 deliveries (table)
     - Columns: Timestamp, Event, Status, Response Time, HTTP Code
     - "View All Deliveries" link
   - Actions:
     - Edit webhook
     - Test webhook
     - View deliveries
     - Configure retry settings
     - Configure security
     - Configure transformations
     - Delete webhook (danger zone)

#### D) Test Webhook

1. User clicks "Test Webhook" button
2. Modal opens:
   - Select event type to test (dropdown of subscribed events)
   - Option to use sample payload or custom payload
   - JSON editor for custom payload (with syntax highlighting)
   - "Send Test Event" button
3. User configures test and clicks "Send Test Event"
4. Backend:
   - Generates test payload
   - Signs payload with webhook secret
   - Sends POST request to webhook URL
   - Records delivery attempt
5. Result modal displays:
   - Status: Success ✓ or Failed ✗
   - HTTP status code
   - Response time
   - Request headers (expandable)
   - Request body (formatted JSON)
   - Response headers (expandable)
   - Response body (formatted)
   - Error message (if failed)
6. Success toast: "Test webhook sent successfully" or "Test webhook failed: {reason}"
7. Test delivery is logged in delivery history with "TEST" label

#### E) View Delivery History

1. User navigates to webhook deliveries page
2. System displays deliveries in chronological order (newest first):
   - Each delivery shows:
     - Timestamp
     - Event type (with icon)
     - Event ID
     - Status indicator (✓ success, ✗ failed, ⟳ retrying)
     - HTTP status code
     - Response time
     - Retry count (if > 0)
     - Quick actions: View details, Retry
3. Features:
   - Filter by:
     - Status (success/failed/retrying)
     - Event type (multi-select)
     - Date range (picker)
     - HTTP status codes
   - Search by event ID
   - Sort by: timestamp, response time, status
   - Pagination (50 per page)
   - Bulk retry failed deliveries
   - Export deliveries (CSV/JSON)
4. Statistics summary at top:
   - Total deliveries: {count}
   - Success rate: {percentage}%
   - Average response time: {ms}
   - Failed deliveries: {count}
5. Real-time updates (via WebSocket or polling every 30s)

#### F) View Delivery Detail

1. User clicks on a specific delivery
2. System displays detailed delivery information:
   - Overview:
     - Status (large badge)
     - Event type
     - Event ID
     - Timestamp
     - Retry count
   - Request section:
     - Method: POST
     - URL: {webhook_url}
     - Headers (expandable list):
       - User-Agent
       - Content-Type
       - X-Skillsier-Signature
       - X-Skillsier-Event
       - X-Skillsier-Delivery-ID
       - (Custom headers if configured)
     - Body (formatted JSON with syntax highlighting)
   - Response section:
     - HTTP status code (colored badge)
     - Response time: {ms}
     - Headers (expandable list)
     - Body (formatted, truncated if large with "Show full response" option)
   - Timing section:
     - Created: {timestamp}
     - Sent: {timestamp}
     - Completed: {timestamp}
     - Total duration: {ms}
   - Retry Information (if applicable):
     - Retry attempt: {current}/{max}
     - Next retry scheduled: {timestamp}
     - Retry history (list of previous attempts)
   - Actions:
     - Retry delivery (if failed)
     - Share delivery details (copy link)
     - Download request/response (JSON)
     - Report issue

#### G) Retry Failed Delivery

1. User clicks "Retry" button on failed delivery
2. Confirmation modal:
   - "Retry this delivery?"
   - Shows: event type, original timestamp, failure reason
   - Option: "Use original payload" or "Edit payload"
3. User confirms
4. Backend:
   - Increments retry count
   - Schedules immediate retry (or adds to retry queue)
   - Sends webhook request
   - Records new delivery attempt
5. User is returned to delivery detail page
6. New attempt appears in retry history
7. Success toast: "Delivery retry initiated" or "Delivery retry failed"

#### H) Configure Retry Settings

1. User navigates to webhook retry configuration page
2. System displays retry policy form:
   - Enable automatic retries toggle (default: ON)
   - Max retry attempts slider (1-10, default: 3)
   - Backoff strategy dropdown:
     - Linear (1s, 2s, 3s, ...)
     - Exponential (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, ...)
     - Fibonacci (1s, 1s, 2s, 3s, 5s, 8s, ...)
   - Initial retry delay input (seconds, default: 1)
   - Max retry delay input (seconds, default: 3600)
   - Retry on HTTP status codes (multi-select):
     - 4xx errors (except 400, 401, 403)
     - All 5xx errors
     - Network timeouts
   - Dead letter queue:
     - Enable DLQ toggle
     - DLQ webhook URL (for permanently failed deliveries)
   - Retry preview timeline visualization:
     - Shows when each retry will occur based on selected strategy
3. User configures settings
4. User clicks "Save Configuration"
5. Backend validates:
   - Delay values are reasonable
   - DLQ URL is valid (if enabled)
6. Backend updates retry policy
7. Success toast: "Retry configuration updated"
8. New policy applies to future failed deliveries

#### I) Configure Security Settings

1. User navigates to webhook security settings page
2. System displays security configuration form:
   - IP Whitelist section:
     - Enable IP restrictions toggle
     - Add IP addresses or CIDR ranges (list)
     - Add/remove IP buttons
     - CIDR validation
   - Rate Limiting section:
     - Enable rate limiting toggle
     - Requests per minute slider (1-1000, default: 100)
     - Requests per hour slider (10-10000, default: 1000)
     - Action on limit exceeded: Queue or Drop
   - Secret Management section:
     - Current secret: "******" (hidden)
     - Show secret (requires re-auth)
     - Regenerate secret button
     - Secret rotation schedule:
       - Auto-rotate: ON/OFF
       - Rotation frequency: Never, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly
   - Signature Algorithm section:
     - Algorithm selector:
       - HMAC-SHA256 (recommended, default)
       - HMAC-SHA512
       - Ed25519
     - Signature header name: X-Skillsier-Signature (default, customizable)
   - Connection Settings section:
     - Request timeout slider (5-120 seconds, default: 30)
     - TLS version requirement: TLS 1.2 (min), TLS 1.3 (recommended)
     - SSL verification: ON (required for production, OFF for testing)
   - Custom Headers section:
     - Add custom headers (key-value pairs)
     - Common presets: Authorization, X-API-Key, etc.
3. User configures security settings
4. User clicks "Save Security Settings"
5. Backend validates:
   - IP addresses/CIDRs are valid
   - Rate limits are reasonable
   - TLS version is supported
6. Backend updates security configuration
7. Success toast: "Security settings updated"
8. If secret regenerated: show new secret once with warning
9. Send email: "Webhook security settings updated for {URL}"

#### J) Configure Payload Transformation

1. User navigates to webhook transformation page
2. System displays transformation configuration:
   - Transformation Rules section:
     - List of transformation rules (ordered)
     - Each rule shows: type, field, action
     - Add/edit/delete/reorder rules
   - Rule Types:
     - Field Mapping: JSONPath selector → new field name
     - Field Rename: old name → new name
     - Field Filter: Include/Exclude specific fields
     - Field Transform: Apply function (uppercase, lowercase, format date, etc.)
     - Conditional Include: Include field only if condition met
   - Custom Headers section:
     - Add headers to transformed payload
   - Payload Template section:
     - JSON template editor
     - Use placeholders: {{event_type}}, {{payload.field_name}}, etc.
     - Template library (common patterns)
   - Transformation Preview:
     - Before panel: original payload (sample)
     - After panel: transformed payload (live preview)
     - Test with sample event button
3. User adds/configures transformation rules:
   - Clicks "Add Rule"
   - Selects rule type
   - Configures rule parameters (e.g., JSONPath selector, new field name)
   - Clicks "Add"
4. User tests transformation:
   - Selects sample event type
   - Clicks "Test Transformation"
   - System applies transformation to sample payload
   - Before/after comparison displayed
5. User clicks "Save Transformation"
6. Backend validates:
   - JSONPath selectors are valid
   - Template syntax is correct
   - No circular references
7. Backend saves transformation configuration
8. Success toast: "Payload transformation saved"
9. New transformation applies to all future deliveries

#### K) Batch Retry Failed Deliveries

1. User navigates to batch retry page
2. System displays failed deliveries summary:
   - Total failed deliveries: {count}
   - Date range: {start} to {end}
   - Top failure reasons (pie chart or bar chart)
3. Filters section:
   - Date range picker
   - Webhook multi-select (if multiple webhooks)
   - Event type filter
   - HTTP status code filter
   - Failure reason filter
4. User applies filters
5. System displays filtered failed deliveries table:
   - Checkboxes for selection
   - Columns: Timestamp, Event, Webhook URL, HTTP Code, Failure Reason
   - "Select All" / "Select None" buttons
6. User selects deliveries to retry (up to 1000 at once)
7. Bulk actions toolbar appears:
   - Selected count indicator: "{X} deliveries selected"
   - "Retry Selected" button
8. User clicks "Retry Selected"
9. Retry options modal:
   - Retry immediately (default)
   - Schedule retry: date/time picker
   - Confirm button
10. User confirms
11. Backend:
    - Queues selected deliveries for retry
    - Processes retries asynchronously
    - Updates delivery statuses
12. Progress indicator shown during batch operation
13. Success toast: "{X} deliveries queued for retry"
14. Real-time progress updates in UI
15. Email notification when batch retry completes: "Batch retry completed: {success_count} succeeded, {failed_count} failed"

#### L) Compare Webhooks

1. User navigates to webhook comparison page
2. Webhook selector: multi-select (max 4 webhooks)
3. User selects 2-4 webhooks to compare
4. System displays side-by-side comparison table:
   - Rows (attributes):
     - URL
     - Status (active/inactive)
     - Events subscribed (count + expandable list)
     - Total deliveries (last 7d)
     - Success rate (last 7d)
     - Avg response time (last 7d)
     - Failed deliveries (last 7d)
     - Retry configuration (strategy, max attempts)
     - Security settings (IP whitelist, rate limit)
     - Secret rotation schedule
     - Last delivery timestamp
   - Columns: one per selected webhook
5. Differences highlighted (e.g., if success rates vary significantly)
6. Actions:
   - Export comparison (CSV/PDF)
   - Copy config from webhook A to webhook B (button per attribute)
   - "Optimize All" button: suggests improvements based on best performer

#### M) Edit Webhook

1. User clicks "Edit" from webhook detail
2. System displays edit form (pre-filled with current values):
   - Webhook URL
   - Description
   - Event subscriptions
   - Active status
   - Custom headers
3. User makes changes
4. User clicks "Save Changes"
5. Backend validates:
   - URL is HTTPS
   - At least one event selected
6. Backend updates webhook
7. Success toast: "Webhook updated successfully"
8. If URL changed: warning modal:
   - "Webhook URL has been changed"
   - "Test the new endpoint to ensure it's working"
   - "Test Webhook" button
9. If events removed: warning:
   - "Removing event subscriptions will stop delivery for those events"
   - List removed events
   - Confirm button

#### N) Delete Webhook

1. User clicks "Delete Webhook" from webhook detail (danger zone)
2. Warning modal:
   - "This action cannot be undone"
   - "All delivery history will be retained for 90 days"
   - Shows statistics: {X} total deliveries, {Y}% success rate
   - Type webhook URL to confirm: input field
3. User types webhook URL
4. User clicks "Delete Webhook"
5. Backend:
   - Soft-deletes webhook (for audit trail)
   - Stops all future deliveries
   - Retains delivery history for 90 days
6. Success toast: "Webhook deleted successfully"
7. Redirect to webhooks list
8. Send email: "Webhook deleted: {URL}"

#### Branches & Edge Cases

**B1: Webhook URL Not Reachable**
- If URL doesn't respond during test ping:
  - Show warning: "Webhook URL is not reachable. Deliveries may fail."
  - Allow creation anyway (user may be setting up endpoint)
  - Suggest: Test webhook after creation

**B2: SSL Certificate Invalid**
- If SSL verification enabled and cert is invalid:
  - Show error: "SSL certificate verification failed"
  - Options:
    - Fix certificate on endpoint
    - Disable SSL verification (not recommended for production)

**B3: Webhook URL is HTTP (Not HTTPS)**
- If URL is HTTP (except localhost):
  - Show error: "Webhook URL must use HTTPS for security"
  - Allow HTTP only for:
    - localhost
    - 127.0.0.1
    - Testing environment (if configured)

**B4: Secret Too Short**
- If custom secret < 32 characters:
  - Show error: "Secret must be at least 32 characters"
  - Suggest: Use auto-generated secret

**B5: No Events Selected**
- If user tries to create webhook with no events:
  - Show error: "At least one event must be selected"
  - Suggest: Select events you want to receive

**B6: Rate Limit Exceeded**
- If webhook deliveries exceed rate limit:
  - If "Queue" action: queue deliveries for later
  - If "Drop" action: drop deliveries and log error
  - Show banner: "Webhook rate limit exceeded. {X} deliveries queued/dropped."
  - Send email: "Webhook rate limit exceeded for {URL}"

**B7: Delivery Timeout**
- If webhook endpoint doesn't respond within timeout:
  - Log as failed delivery with reason: "Request timeout"
  - Retry according to retry policy
  - If max retries exceeded: send to DLQ (if configured) or mark as permanently failed

**B8: Signature Verification Failed**
- If signature in request doesn't match:
  - Endpoint should reject with 401 Unauthorized
  - Skillsier logs this as delivery failure
  - If repeated: send security alert email

**B9: Max Retry Attempts Exceeded**
- After max retries:
  - Mark delivery as "permanently failed"
  - If DLQ configured: send to DLQ webhook
  - Send email notification: "Webhook delivery permanently failed for event {event_id}"
  - Suggest: Check endpoint health, review logs

**B10: IP Whitelist Restriction**
- If IP whitelist enabled and request from unknown IP:
  - Reject request before sending
  - Log: "Delivery blocked: IP not whitelisted"
  - Don't count against retry attempts
  - Suggest: Add IP to whitelist or disable restriction

**B11: Payload Too Large**
- If event payload exceeds size limit (e.g., 1MB):
  - Show warning: "Payload size exceeds limit"
  - Options:
    - Configure transformation to filter fields
    - Use pagination for large payloads
    - Store payload in S3 and send URL instead

**B12: Circular Transformation Reference**
- If transformation rules create circular reference:
  - Show error: "Transformation rules contain circular reference"
  - Highlight conflicting rules
  - Suggest: Remove or reorder rules

**B13: Webhook Not Used (30 Days)**
- If webhook hasn't received any events in 30 days:
  - Send email: "Your webhook {URL} hasn't received events in 30 days. Consider removing it if no longer needed."

**B14: High Failure Rate**
- If webhook failure rate > 50% over 7 days:
  - Show banner: "High failure rate detected for this webhook"
  - Send email: "Webhook health alert: {URL} has {percentage}% failure rate"
  - Suggest: Review endpoint logs, check retry configuration

**B15: Secret Rotation Scheduled**
- If auto-rotation enabled:
  - 7 days before: email notification: "Webhook secret will be rotated in 7 days for {URL}"
  - On rotation day:
    - Generate new secret
    - Send email with new secret (one time)
    - Grace period: old secret valid for 24 hours
    - After 24h: old secret invalid

#### Notifications

**Webhook Created:**
- **Email:** "Webhook created: {URL}. Subscribed to {X} events. Keep your secret secure."
- **In-app:** Toast: "Webhook created successfully"

**Webhook Updated:**
- **Email:** "Webhook updated: {URL}. Review changes in your dashboard."
- **In-app:** Toast: "Webhook updated successfully"

**Webhook Deleted:**
- **Email:** "Webhook deleted: {URL}. Delivery history retained for 90 days."
- **In-app:** Toast: "Webhook deleted successfully"

**Webhook Test Sent:**
- **In-app:** Toast: "Test webhook sent" or "Test webhook failed: {reason}"

**Delivery Failed:**
- **In-app (after 3 consecutive failures):** Notification: "Webhook deliveries failing for {URL}. {X} failures in last hour."
- **Email (after 10 consecutive failures):** "Webhook delivery failures detected: {URL}. Check endpoint health."

**Delivery Permanently Failed:**
- **Email:** "Webhook delivery permanently failed for event {event_id}. Max retries exceeded."
- **In-app:** Notification: "Delivery permanently failed"

**Batch Retry Complete:**
- **Email:** "Batch retry completed: {success_count} succeeded, {failed_count} failed out of {total_count} deliveries."
- **In-app:** Toast: "Batch retry completed"

**Secret Rotated:**
- **Email (urgent):** "Webhook secret rotated for {URL}. New secret: {secret}. Update your signature verification immediately. Old secret valid for 24 hours."
- **In-app:** Toast: "Secret rotated successfully"

**Secret Rotation Scheduled:**
- **Email (7 days before):** "Webhook secret will be auto-rotated in 7 days for {URL}. Prepare to update your integration."
- **Email (1 day before):** "Webhook secret will be auto-rotated tomorrow for {URL}."

**High Failure Rate Alert:**
- **Email:** "Webhook health alert: {URL} has {percentage}% failure rate over last 7 days. {failed_count} failed deliveries."
- **In-app:** Banner: "High failure rate detected for this webhook"

**Rate Limit Exceeded:**
- **Email:** "Webhook rate limit exceeded for {URL}. {X} deliveries queued/dropped."
- **In-app:** Banner: "Rate limit exceeded. Adjust limits or upgrade plan."

**Security Alert:**
- **Email (urgent):** "Security alert for webhook {URL}: {reason} (e.g., repeated signature verification failures, unauthorized IP attempts)"
- **In-app:** Alert: "Security alert: Review webhook activity"

..6
**Webhook Inactive (30 Days):**
- **Email:** "Your webhook {URL} hasn't received events in 30 days. Remove if no longer needed."

## DEV-4 — API Sandbox / Testing

**ID:** DEV-4  
**Persona:** Developer, API Consumer  
**Preconditions:** User has developer access, API key created  
**Triggers:** Navigate to developer/sandbox, Test API endpoints  

### Primary Screens

**Web:**
- `(dashboard)/developer/sandbox/page.tsx` — API sandbox main
- `(dashboard)/developer/sandbox/environments/page.tsx` — Test environments
- `(dashboard)/developer/sandbox/test-data/page.tsx` — Test data management
- `(dashboard)/developer/sandbox/collections/page.tsx` — Request collections
- `(dashboard)/developer/sandbox/collections/[collectionId]/page.tsx` — Collection detail

**Mobile:**
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/developer/sandbox/index.tsx` — API sandbox
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/developer/sandbox/collections/index.tsx` — Collections list

#### System Touchpoints

**Backend:** All microservices (via API Gateway), users-be (sandbox environment management)  
**APIs:**
- GET /v1/developer/sandbox/environments
- POST /v1/developer/sandbox/environments
- DELETE /v1/developer/sandbox/environments/{env_id}
- POST /v1/developer/sandbox/environments/{env_id}/reset
- GET /v1/developer/sandbox/test-data
- POST /v1/developer/sandbox/test-data
- DELETE /v1/developer/sandbox/test-data/{data_id}
- GET /v1/developer/sandbox/collections
- POST /v1/developer/sandbox/collections
- GET /v1/developer/sandbox/collections/{collection_id}
- PUT /v1/developer/sandbox/collections/{collection_id}
- DELETE /v1/developer/sandbox/collections/{collection_id}
- POST /v1/developer/sandbox/execute (execute sandbox requests)

**Plus all Skillsier API endpoints** (for testing)

#### Flow Steps

#### A) Access API Sandbox

1. User navigates to developer/sandbox
2. System displays interactive API testing interface:
   - Top bar:
     - Environment selector (Production, Sandbox, Custom)
     - API key selector (dropdown of user's API keys)
     - Base URL display (read-only, changes with environment)
   - Left sidebar:
     - Endpoint explorer (tree view):
       - Grouped by resource (Users, Jobs, Proposals, Contracts, etc.)
       - Each endpoint shows: Method (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE), Path
       - Search/filter endpoints
       - Favorites (star icon)
   - Main area:
     - Request builder (detailed below)
   - Right sidebar:
     - Response viewer (detailed below)
   - Bottom bar:
     - Request history (last 50 requests)
     - Collections shortcut

#### B) Build API Request

1. User selects endpoint from explorer OR enters custom endpoint
2. Request builder displays:
   - Method selector: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
   - Endpoint input: /v1/users/{user_id}/profile
   - Path parameters section (if applicable):
     - Auto-detected from endpoint (e.g., {user_id})
     - Input fields for each parameter
   - Query parameters section:
     - Key-value pairs (add/remove rows)
     - Common parameters auto-suggested (page, limit, sort, etc.)
   - Headers section:
     - Key-value pairs
     - Auth headers auto-populated from selected API key:
       - Authorization: Bearer {api_key}
       - X-API-Key: {api_key} (depending on auth method)
     - Custom headers can be added
   - Body section (for POST/PUT/PATCH):
     - Content-Type selector: JSON, form-data, x-www-form-urlencoded
     - JSON editor with:
       - Syntax highlighting
       - Line numbers
       - Auto-completion (based on endpoint schema if available)
       - Format/minify buttons
       - Validation (shows errors inline)
     - Form-data editor (key-value with file upload support)
3. User fills in request parameters
4. Schema validation (if available):
   - Real-time validation against OpenAPI spec
   - Highlights missing required fields
   - Suggests valid values for enums

#### C) Execute API Request

1. User clicks "Send Request" button (large, prominent)
2. System shows loading indicator
3. Backend (sandbox service):
   - Validates request structure
   - Adds necessary auth headers
   - Executes request against selected environment
   - Records request/response for history
4. Response viewer (right sidebar) displays:
   - Status section (top):
     - HTTP status code (colored badge: green for 2xx, yellow for 3xx, red for 4xx/5xx)
     - Status text (OK, Created, Bad Request, etc.)
     - Response time: {ms}
     - Response size: {kb}
   - Tabs:
     - **Body tab:**
       - Formatted JSON (syntax highlighted, collapsible sections)
       - Raw view toggle
       - Copy button
       - Download button (saves as JSON file)
     - **Headers tab:**
       - List of response headers (key-value pairs)
       - Copy button per header
     - **Cookies tab:**
       - List of cookies set by response
     - **Timing tab:**
       - Breakdown of request timing:
         - DNS lookup: {ms}
         - TCP connection: {ms}
         - TLS handshake: {ms}
         - Request sent: {ms}
         - Waiting (TTFB): {ms}
         - Content download: {ms}
       - Waterfall chart visualization
5. If request failed:
   - Error message prominently displayed
   - Error details (if available from API)
   - Suggestions for fixing (e.g., "Check API key permissions", "Verify request body format")

#### D) Save Request to Collection

1. After executing a request, user clicks "Save to Collection" button
2. Modal opens:
   - Collection selector:
     - Dropdown of existing collections
     - "Create New Collection" option
   - Request name input (auto-populated with "{Method} {Endpoint}", editable)
   - Description textarea (optional)
   - Tags input (comma-separated, for organization)
3. If creating new collection:
   - Collection name input
   - Collection description
4. User clicks "Save"
5. Backend saves request configuration:
   - Method, endpoint, headers, body, query params
   - Expected response (optional, for comparison)
6. Success toast: "Request saved to collection '{name}'"
7. Request appears in collections sidebar

#### E) Use Request Collections

1. User navigates to developer/sandbox/collections
2. System displays list of collections:
   - Each collection shows:
     - Name, description
     - Request count
     - Last modified date
     - Favorite icon
     - Quick actions: Open, Edit, Duplicate, Delete
3. User clicks on a collection
4. Collection detail page displays:
   - Collection info (name, description, tags)
   - List of requests in collection:
     - Request name
     - Method + Endpoint
     - Last executed timestamp
     - Success/failure indicator
     - Quick actions: Execute, Edit, Duplicate, Delete
   - Actions:
     - Run all requests (sequence)
     - Export collection (JSON format compatible with Postman/Insomnia)
     - Import requests (from JSON file)
     - Share collection (generate shareable link with view-only access)
5. User clicks "Execute" on a specific request
6. System loads request configuration into sandbox
7. Request is auto-populated with saved parameters
8. User can modify and execute, or execute as-is

#### F) Manage Test Environments

1. User navigates to developer/sandbox/environments
2. System displays available environments:
   - Production:
     - Base URL: https://api.skillsier.com
     - Description: Live production environment
     - Badge: LIVE (cannot be deleted)
   - Sandbox (default):
     - Base URL: https://sandbox.api.skillsier.com
     - Description: Isolated testing environment with sample data
     - Badge: SANDBOX
   - Custom environments (user-created):
     - Each shows: Name, Base URL, Description, Created date
3. Create custom environment:
   - User clicks "Create Environment"
   - Modal with form:
     - Environment name (required)
     - Base URL (required, must be valid URL)
     - Description (optional)
     - API key (can use existing or enter custom)
   - User fills form and clicks "Create"
   - Backend validates and creates environment
   - Success toast: "Environment created: {name}"
4. Edit environment:
   - User clicks "Edit" on custom environment
   - Modal with pre-filled form
   - User makes changes and saves
5. Delete environment:
   - User clicks "Delete" on custom environment
   - Confirmation modal: "Delete environment '{name}'? This cannot be undone."
   - User confirms
   - Backend deletes environment
   - Success toast: "Environment deleted"
6. Reset sandbox environment:
   - User clicks "Reset" on Sandbox environment
   - Warning modal:
     - "This will delete all test data and reset the sandbox to its default state"
     - "All test users, jobs, contracts will be removed"
     - Type "RESET" to confirm
   - User types "RESET" and confirms
   - Backend resets sandbox (async operation)
   - Progress indicator shown
   - Success toast: "Sandbox environment reset successfully"
   - Email notification: "Sandbox environment has been reset"

#### G) Manage Test Data

1. User navigates to developer/sandbox/test-data
2. System displays test data management interface:
   - Available test data templates:
     - Users (clients, freelancers, admins)
     - Organizations
     - Jobs (various statuses)
     - Proposals
     - Contracts
     - Payments
     - Messages
   - Current test data summary:
     - Count of each entity type in sandbox
     - Last generated: timestamp
3. Generate test data:
   - User selects template(s) to generate
   - Configuration modal:
     - Quantity slider (how many entities to create)
     - Relationships toggle (create related entities, e.g., proposals for jobs)
     - Randomization options (names, dates, amounts)
   - User clicks "Generate"
   - Backend generates test data asynchronously
   - Progress indicator shown
   - Success toast: "Test data generated: {X} users, {Y} jobs, etc."
4. Import test data:
   - User clicks "Import Data"
   - File upload dialog (JSON format)
   - Backend validates JSON structure
   - If valid: imports data into sandbox
   - Success toast: "Test data imported successfully"
5. Export test data:
   - User clicks "Export Data"
   - Options: All data, or select entity types
   - Format: JSON (default), CSV
   - Backend exports data
   - File download initiated
   - Success toast: "Test data exported"
6. Clear test data:
   - User clicks "Clear All Test Data" (danger zone)
   - Warning modal: "This will delete all test data. Type 'DELETE' to confirm."
   - User types "DELETE" and confirms
   - Backend deletes test data
   - Success toast: "Test data cleared"

#### H) View Request History

1. Request history panel (bottom of sandbox page) shows last 50 requests
2. Each history entry shows:
   - Timestamp (relative: "2 minutes ago")
   - Method + Endpoint (truncated)
   - Status code (colored)
   - Response time
3. User can:
   - Click to reload request into sandbox
   - Star to save to favorites
   - Delete from history
4. Filters:
   - By method (GET, POST, etc.)
   - By status (2xx, 4xx, 5xx)
   - By endpoint (search)
   - By date range
5. History is persisted (stored in backend)
6. Auto-pruned after 30 days

#### I) Use Code Snippets

1. After executing a request, user clicks "Code" button
2. Code snippet modal opens
3. Language selector: cURL, JavaScript (fetch), Python (requests), PHP (cURL), Ruby (Net::HTTP), Go (http)
4. System generates code snippet for selected language:
   - Includes all headers, body, query params
   - Auth headers included (with API key)
   - Properly formatted and escaped
5. Copy button copies snippet to clipboard
6. Download button saves as file (with appropriate extension)
7. Success toast: "Code snippet copied"

#### J) Compare API Responses

1. User executes a request and sees response
2. User clicks "Compare" button
3. "Compare with" options:
   - Expected response (if saved in collection)
   - Previous response (from history)
   - Custom response (paste JSON)
4. User selects comparison source
5. System displays diff view:
   - Side-by-side comparison (left: actual, right: comparison)
   - Differences highlighted:
     - Green: added fields/values
     - Red: removed fields/values
     - Yellow: modified values
   - Navigation buttons: Previous diff, Next diff
6. Metrics shown:
   - Fields added: {count}
   - Fields removed: {count}
   - Fields modified: {count}
   - Similarity score: {percentage}%

#### Branches & Edge Cases

**B1: Invalid API Key**
- If selected API key is invalid or expired:
  - Show error: "API key is invalid or expired. Select a different key or create a new one."
  - Suggest: Navigate to API keys page

**B2: Endpoint Not Found (404)**
- If endpoint doesn't exist:
  - Show error in response: "404 Not Found"
  - Suggest: "Check endpoint spelling. View API documentation."

**B3: Request Timeout**
- If request exceeds timeout (30s default):
  - Show error: "Request timeout. The server did not respond in time."
  - Suggest: "Try again or increase timeout in settings"

**B4: Malformed JSON in Body**
- If JSON is invalid:
  - Show error inline in editor (red squiggly underline)
  - Error message: "Invalid JSON: {error details}"
  - Prevent request execution until fixed
  - "Format JSON" button available to attempt auto-fix

**B5: Missing Required Parameters**
- If schema validation detects missing required fields:
  - Highlight missing fields in red
  - Show error message: "Missing required parameter: {field_name}"
  - Prevent request execution

**B6: Rate Limit Exceeded**
- If API rate limit hit:
  - Response: 429 Too Many Requests
  - Show error: "Rate limit exceeded. Try again in {X} seconds."
  - Display Retry-After header value

**B7: Unauthorized (401)**
- If API key lacks permissions:
  - Response: 401 Unauthorized
  - Show error: "Unauthorized. Check API key permissions."
  - Suggest: "Update API key scopes or use a different key"

**B8: Large Response Body**
- If response > 5MB:
  - Show warning: "Response is large ({size}MB). Viewing may be slow."
  - Option to download instead of viewing
  - Paginate or virtualize response viewer

**B9: Binary Response**
- If response is binary (PDF, image, etc.):
  - Detect Content-Type
  - Show message: "Binary response detected"
  - Options:
    - Download file
    - View as base64 (for images, show preview)

**B10: Network Error**
- If network connection fails:
  - Show error: "Network error. Check your connection."
  - Suggest: "Retry request"

**B11: Collection Limit Exceeded**
- If user reaches collection limit (e.g., 100 collections):
  - Show error: "Collection limit reached. Delete unused collections."

**B12: Sandbox Reset in Progress**
- If user tries to use sandbox during reset:
  - Show banner: "Sandbox is being reset. Requests will fail temporarily."
  - Disable request execution
  - Show progress indicator

#### Notifications

**Request Executed:**
- **In-app:** Toast: "Request executed in {X}ms" (only if user has notifications enabled)

**Request Saved to Collection:**
- **In-app:** Toast: "Request saved to collection '{name}'"

**Collection Created:**
- **In-app:** Toast: "Collection created: {name}"

**Collection Exported:**
- **In-app:** Toast: "Collection exported successfully"
- **Email (optional):** "API collection '{name}' exported. Download link: {URL}"

**Test Data Generated:**
- **In-app:** Toast: "Test data generated: {X} entities created"

**Sandbox Environment Reset:**
- **Email:** "Sandbox environment has been reset. All test data has been cleared."
- **In-app:** Toast: "Sandbox reset complete"

**Environment Created:**
- **In-app:** Toast: "Environment created: {name}"

**Code Snippet Copied:**
- **In-app:** Toast: "Code snippet copied to clipboard"

- developer.sandbox.request_executed (user_id, method, endpoint, status_code, response_time_ms, environment)
- developer.sandbox.request_failed (user_id, method, endpoint, error_reason)
- developer.sandbox.request_saved (user_id, collection_id, request_name)
- developer.sandbox.collection_created (user_id, collection_id, request_count)
- developer.sandbox.collection_exported (user_id, collection_id, format)
- developer.sandbox.collection_imported (user_id, request_count)
- developer.sandbox.code_snippet_generated (user_id, language, endpoint)

- developer.sandbox.environment_created (user_id, environment_id, base_url)

   - **Step 3: Make Your First Request**
     - Example: GET /v1/users/me (get current user)
     - Code samples in multiple languages:
       ```bash
       # cURL
       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
            https://api.skillsier.com/v1/users/me
       ```
       ```javascript
       // JavaScript (fetch)
       const response = await fetch('https://api.skillsier.com/v1/users/me', {
         headers: {
           'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_API_KEY'
         }
       });
       const user = await response.json();
       ```
       ```python
       # Python (requests)
       import requests
       response = requests.get(
         'https://api.skillsier.com/v1/users/me',
         headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_API_KEY'}
       )
       user = response.json()
       ```
     - "Try It Now" button: opens sandbox with pre-filled request
   - **Step 4: Handle Responses**
     - Success response example (200 OK):
       ```json
       {
         "user_id": "uuid",
         "email": "user@example.com",
         "name": "John Doe",
         "user_type": "FREELANCER",
         "verified": true
       }
       ```
     - Error response example (401 Unauthorized):
       ```json

         "error": {
           "code": "UNAUTHORIZED",
           "message": "Invalid or expired API key",

         }
       ```

#### F) View Webhooks Guide

       - Event name (e.g., job.created.v1)

   - **Receiving Webhooks:**
     - Endpoint requirements (HTTPS, response codes)
     - Payload structure:
       ```json
       {
         "event_id": "uuid",
         "event_type": "job.created.v1",
         "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",

           "job_id": "uuid",
           "title": "...",
           ...
         }
       }
       ```
     - Response expectations (200 OK within 5 seconds)
   - **Signature Verification:**
     - How signatures work (HMAC-SHA256)
     - Verification code examples:
       ```javascript
       const crypto = require('crypto');
       
       function verifySignature(payload, signature, secret) {
         const hmac = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret);
         const digest = hmac.update(payload).digest('hex');
         return signature === digest;
       }
       ```
     - Best practices: always verify signatures
   - **Retry Logic:**
     - How Skillsier retries failed deliveries
     - Exponential backoff strategy
     - Max retry attempts
     - Dead letter queue

#### G) View Error Handling Guide

1. User navigates to Error Handling documentation
2. System displays error handling guide:
   - **HTTP Status Codes:**
     - 200 OK: Successful request
     - 201 Created: Resource created
     - 204 No Content: Successful delete
     - 400 Bad Request: Invalid parameters
     - 401 Unauthorized: Invalid/missing API key
     - 403 Forbidden: Insufficient permissions
     - 404 Not Found: Resource doesn't exist
     - 409 Conflict: Resource conflict
     - 429 Too Many Requests: Rate limit exceeded
     - 500 Internal Server Error: Server error
     - 503 Service Unavailable: Maintenance/overload
   - **Error Response Format:**
     ```json
     {
       "error": {
         "code": "ERROR_CODE",
         "message": "Human-readable error message",
         "details": {
           "field": "additional context"
         },
         "request_id": "uuid"
       }
     }
     ```
   - **Error Codes Reference:**
     - Complete list of error codes with descriptions
     - INVALID_PARAMETER
     - MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD
     - RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND
     - UNAUTHORIZED
     - INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS
     - RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
     - (All other error codes)
   - **Handling Errors:**
     - Best practices code examples:
       ```javascript
       try {
         const response = await fetch(url, options);
         if (!response.ok) {
           const error = await response.json();
           console.error('API Error:', error.error.code, error.error.message);
           // Handle specific errors
           if (error.error.code === 'RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED') {
             // Wait and retry
           }
         }
       } catch (err) {
         console.error('Network error:', err);
       }
       ```
   - **Retry Strategy:**
     - When to retry (5xx errors, timeouts)
     - When not to retry (4xx errors except 429)
     - Exponential backoff example
   - **Request IDs:**
     - Every response includes a request_id
     - Use request_id when contacting support
     - How to pass request_id in logs

#### H) View Rate Limits Guide

1. User navigates to Rate Limits documentation
2. System displays rate limits guide:
   - **Overview:**
     - Why rate limits exist
     - Types of limits (per API key, per user, per endpoint)
   - **Current Limits:**
     - Table showing limits by plan tier:
       | Plan | Requests/Hour | Requests/Day | Burst Limit |
       |------|---------------|--------------|-------------|
       | Free | 100 | 1,000 | 10/min |
       | Basic | 1,000 | 10,000 | 50/min |
       | Pro | 10,000 | 100,000 | 200/min |
       | Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom |
   - **Rate Limit Headers:**
     - Every response includes:
       - `X-RateLimit-Limit`: Total requests allowed
       - `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: Requests remaining
       - `X-RateLimit-Reset`: Timestamp when limit resets
     - Example:
       ```
       X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
       X-RateLimit-Remaining: 950
       X-RateLimit-Reset: 1642684800
       ```
   - **Handling Rate Limits:**
     - Check headers before making requests
     - Implement exponential backoff when rate limited
     - Use webhook subscriptions instead of polling
     - Cache responses when possible
     - Batch requests when supported
   - **Rate Limit Exceeded Response:**
     - Status: 429 Too Many Requests
     - Response body:
       ```json
       {
         "error": {
           "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
           "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 60 seconds.",
           "retry_after": 60
         }
       }
       ```
   - **Best Practices:**
     - Monitor your usage
     - Implement request throttling
     - Use pagination efficiently
     - Avoid unnecessary requests
   - **Upgrade Options:**
     - Link to pricing page
     - Contact sales for enterprise limits

       - Change: +0.3%

     - Average Response Time:
       - Value: 145ms
       - Change: -8ms
       - Mini chart
     - Rate Limit Usage:
       - Current: 45% of limit
       - Bar chart showing usage
       - Next reset: 2h 15m
   - **Requests Over Time Chart:**
     - Line chart showing requests per hour/day
     - Multiple lines: Total, Successful, Failed
     - Hover to see exact values
     - Click to drill down
   - **Top Endpoints Table:**
     - Columns: Endpoint, Method, Requests, Success Rate, Avg Response Time
     - Sort by any column
     - Pagination (top 10 by default, "View All" button)
   - **Errors Breakdown:**
     - Pie chart showing error types (4xx vs 5xx)
     - List of top errors by count:
       - 401 Unauthorized: 45 requests
       - 404 Not Found: 23 requests
       - 429 Rate Limit Exceeded: 12 requests
       - (Others)
     - "View Error Details" button
   - **Geographic Distribution:**
     - World map showing requests by country
     - Table: Country, Requests, Percentage
     - Sort by requests
   - **API Keys Performance:**
     - Table showing each API key:
       - Key name (partial key)
       - Requests
       - Success rate
       - Last used
     - "View Details" link per key
   - **Quick Actions:**
     - Export usage data (CSV/JSON)
     - View detailed reports
     - Set up usage alerts

#### B) View Per-Key Analytics

1. User navigates to developer/usage/api-keys
2. System displays all API keys with usage stats:
   - Table columns:
     - API Key Name
     - Key ID (partial)
     - Total Requests (selected period)
     - Success Rate
     - Error Count
     - Average Response Time
     - Last Used
     - Status (Active/Revoked)
   - Actions per key:
     - View detailed analytics
     - View logs
     - Download report
3. User clicks "View Details" on a specific key
4. System navigates to single key analytics page (detailed below)

#### C) View Single API Key Detailed Analytics

1. User navigates to developer/usage/api-keys/[keyId]
2. System displays detailed analytics for the specific key:
   - **Key Overview:**

     - Last used
     - Status
     - Permissions
   - **Usage Summary:**
     - Total requests (selected period)
     - Successful requests
     - Failed requests
     - Success rate
     - Average response time
   - **Requests Over Time:**
     - Line chart (hourly or daily)

   - **Endpoint Usage:**
     - Bar chart showing requests per endpoint
     - Table with details:
       - Endpoint
       - Method
       - Requests
       - Success Rate
       - Avg Response Time
       - Top Errors
   - **Response Time Distribution:**

#### D) View Webhook Analytics

1. User navigates to developer/usage/webhooks

#### E) View Error Analytics

1. User navigates to developer/usage/errors
2. System displays error analytics:
   - **Error Overview:**

     - Error Rate (% of total requests)
     - Top Error Codes
     - New Errors (first seen in period)
   - **Errors Over Time:**
     - Stacked area chart: 4xx errors, 5xx errors
   - **Error Code Breakdown:**
     - Table:

       - % of Total Errors

       - Last Seen
       - Trend (up/down arrow)

     - Error description
     - Common causes
     - How to fix

       - Timestamp
       - API Key
       - Endpoint
       - Request Details (expandable)
       - Response (expandable)
   - **Top Endpoints with Errors:**
     - Table: Endpoint, Error Count, Error Rate
   - **Client Error Analysis:**
     - User agents causing most errors
     - IPs causing most errors (potential abuse detection)
   - **Recommendations:**
     - Based on error patterns, suggest:
       - Update SDK version (if outdated SDK detected)
       - Check authentication (if many 401s)
       - Review rate limits (if many 429s)
       - Update request parameters (if many 400s)

#### F) Create Custom Report

1. User navigates to developer/usage/reports
2. System displays custom reports interface:
   - **Report Builder:**
     - Report Name input
     - Date Range selector
     - Metrics to Include (checkboxes):
       - Total Requests
       - Success Rate
       - Error Rate
       - Response Time (avg, median, P95, P99)

       - Error Breakdown

       - (All available metrics)

       - API Keys (multi-select)
       - Endpoints (multi-select)
       - Status Codes (multi-select)
       - Countries (multi-select)

     - Export Format (CSV, JSON, PDF)
   - **Preview:**
     - Show sample data based on selections
     - Table or chart preview
   - **Actions:**
     - Generate Report
     - Schedule Report (recurring)
     - Save Report Template
3. User clicks "Generate Report"
4. System generates report:
   - Progress indicator
   - Report generated
   - Display results inline
   - Download button
   - Share button (generate shareable link with expiry)

#### G) Schedule Recurring Report

1. User clicks "Schedule Report" in custom reports
2. Modal opens:
   - Report Configuration (as above)
   - Schedule Settings:
     - Frequency: Daily, Weekly, Monthly
     - Day/Time: Select when to generate
     - Email To: Input email addresses (comma-separated)
     - Format: CSV, JSON, PDF
   - User saves schedule
3. Backend:
   - Creates scheduled job
   - Sends report via email at specified interval
4. User receives email:
   - Subject: "Skillsier API Usage Report - [Date]"
   - Body: Brief summary + download link
   - Report attached or available via link

#### H) Set Up Usage Alerts

1. User clicks "Set Up Alerts" in usage dashboard
2. System displays alerts configuration page:
   - **Available Alerts:**
     - Rate Limit Approaching:
       - Threshold: 80% (slider)
       - Notification: Email + In-app
     - Error Rate Spike:
       - Threshold: Error rate > 5% (input)
       - Notification: Email + In-app + SMS (optional)
     - Unusual Traffic Pattern:
       - Detect anomalies using ML
       - Notification: Email + In-app
     - Webhook Delivery Failures:
       - Threshold: > 10 failures in 1 hour
       - Notification: Email
     - New Error Type Detected:
       - Alert on first occurrence of new error
       - Notification: Email + In-app
     - API Key Not Used (X days):
       - Threshold: 30 days (input)
       - Notification: Email
   - For each alert:
     - Enable/Disable toggle
     - Configure threshold
     - Select notification channels
     - Set cooldown period (to avoid alert spam)
3. User configures alerts and saves
4. When alert triggered:
   - Send notifications via selected channels
   - In-app notification: "⚠️ Alert: Rate limit approaching 80%"
   - Email: "Skillsier API Alert: [Alert Name]"
   - SMS (if configured): "Skillsier API Alert: [Brief Message]"

#### I) Compare API Keys Performance

1. From per-key analytics page, user clicks "Compare with other keys"
2. Modal opens:
   - Multi-select: Choose keys to compare (up to 5)
3. User selects 2-5 keys and clicks "Compare"
4. System displays side-by-side comparison:
   - Comparison table:
     - Rows: Metrics (Requests, Success Rate, Avg Response Time, Errors, etc.)
     - Columns: Each selected key
   - Charts:
     - Overlaid line charts (requests over time per key)
     - Grouped bar charts (metrics comparison)
   - Insights:
     - Highlight key with best performance
     - Identify outliers
     - Suggest optimizations

#### J) Export Usage Data

1. User clicks "Export" button in any analytics view
2. Export modal opens:
   - Date Range selector
   - Data to Export (checkboxes):
     - Request logs
     - Summary statistics
     - Error logs
     - Webhook deliveries
     - Custom metrics
   - Format:
     - CSV (default)
     - JSON
     - PDF (report)
   - Advanced Options:
     - Include headers: Yes/No
     - Delimiter (for CSV): Comma, Semicolon, Tab
     - Compress (ZIP): Yes/No
3. User clicks "Export"
4. System:
   - Generates export file
   - Progress indicator shown
   - When complete: download link provided
   - File available for 7 days
5. Success toast: "Export complete. Download your file."

#### Branches & Edge Cases

**B1: No Usage Data Yet**
- If user has created API keys but no requests yet:
  - Show empty state:
    - Illustration
    - Message: "No usage data yet. Make your first API request to see analytics."
    - "Getting Started" CTA button

**B2: Large Data Set (Slow Query)**
- If date range too large or data too complex:
  - Show loading indicator: "Fetching large dataset. This may take a moment..."
  - If exceeds timeout (30s):
    - Show message: "This query is taking longer than expected. Try a smaller date range or export the data for offline analysis."
    - Suggest: Narrow date range, use filters

**B3: Rate Limit Data Not Available**
- If rate limit data not yet tracked (legacy keys):
  - Show message: "Rate limit data not available for this key. Regenerate key to enable tracking."

**B4: Export Too Large**
- If export exceeds size limit (e.g., 100MB):
  - Show error: "Export too large. Please narrow your date range or contact support for assistance."
  - Suggest: Split into multiple exports

**B5: Alert Notification Failure**
- If email/SMS fails to send:
  - Log failure
  - Show in-app notification as backup
  - Retry sending after 5 minutes
  - If still fails: show warning in dashboard

**B6: No Errors to Display**
- If error rate is 0%:
  - Show success message: "🎉 Great job! No errors detected in the selected period."
  - Encourage: Keep up the good work

**B7: Webhook Endpoint Unreachable**
- If webhook endpoint consistently fails:
  - Show alert: "Webhook endpoint {URL} appears to be unreachable. {X} consecutive failures."
  - Suggest: Check endpoint health, review logs

#### Notifications

**Usage Alert Triggered:**
- **Email:** "Skillsier API Alert: [Alert Name]. [Details]. [Action Link]"
- **In-app:** Notification with link to analytics
- **SMS (if configured):** "Skillsier API Alert: [Brief Message]"

**Report Generated (Scheduled):**
- **Email:** "Your Skillsier API Usage Report is Ready. [Download Link or Attachment]"

**Export Complete:**
- **In-app:** Toast: "Export complete. Your file is ready for download."

**Rate Limit Approaching:**
- **Email:** "Your API key is approaching its rate limit (80% used). Upgrade or wait for reset."
- **In-app:** Banner: "Rate limit approaching"

**Unusual Activity Detected:**
- **Email (urgent):** "Unusual API activity detected for key {name}. Review immediately."
- **In-app:** Alert: "Security alert: Unusual activity"

**New Error Type Detected:**
- **Email:** "New error type detected: {error_code}. First seen: {timestamp}."
- **In-app:** Notification with link to error details

# Section L: Admin / Moderation

---

### **ADM-1 — Admin Dashboard & System Monitoring**

**ID:** ADM-1  
**Persona:** Platform Admin, System Administrator  
**Preconditions:**
- User has ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN role
- User authenticated and authorized
- Admin dashboard permissions granted

**Primary Screens:**

**Web:**
- `(dashboard)/admin` — Admin dashboard overview
- `(dashboard)/admin/system/health` — System health monitoring
- `(dashboard)/admin/system/metrics` — System metrics & analytics
- `(dashboard)/admin/system/alerts` — System alerts & notifications

**Mobile:**
- `(dashboard)/admin` — Admin dashboard (responsive)
- `(dashboard)/admin/system` — System monitoring (mobile-optimized)

**System Touchpoints:**
- **admin-be:** Health monitoring, metrics aggregation, system configuration
- **utility:** Analytics service for system metrics
- **Redis:** Caching for real-time metrics

**Flow Steps:**

1. **Access Admin Dashboard**
   - Admin navigates to `(dashboard)/admin`
   - System validates ADMIN role permissions
   - Dashboard loads with key metrics overview

2. **View System Health**
   - Admin views system health status
   - Real-time metrics display:
     - Service uptime & availability
     - Response times (P50, P95, P99)
     - Error rates by service
     - Active connections
     - Database health
     - Cache hit rates

3. **Monitor Critical Metrics**
   - Platform-wide KPIs displayed:
     - Active users (last 24h, 7d, 30d)
     - Job postings (active, filled, pending)
     - Contracts (active, completed, disputed)
     - Financial volume (escrow, payments, withdrawals)
     - Support ticket volume
     - Moderation queue size

4. **View Alerts & Notifications**
   - System alerts displayed by priority:
     - CRITICAL: Service outages, security breaches
     - HIGH: Performance degradation, high error rates
     - MEDIUM: Resource warnings, quota approaching
     - LOW: Informational updates
   - Admin can acknowledge or escalate alerts

5. **Drill Down into Specific Metrics**
   - Click on any metric for detailed view
   - Time-series graphs (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d)
   - Comparison to historical baselines
   - Anomaly detection highlights

**Branches & Edge Cases:**

**B1: Service Degradation Detected**
- Dashboard shows RED status for affected service
- Alert banner: "Service Degradation Detected: {service_name}"
- Auto-refresh every 30 seconds
- Incident timeline displayed
- Link to incident management

**B2: Multiple Critical Alerts**
- Alert aggregation by category
- Priority sorting (CRITICAL first)
- Quick actions: "Acknowledge All", "Create Incident"
- Escalation path shown

**B3: Historical Data Not Available**
- Show message: "Historical data loading... This may take a moment."
- Graceful degradation: Show current metrics only
- Option to export data for offline analysis

**B4: Permission Denied for Specific Section**
- Hide restricted sections
- Show lock icon with tooltip: "Requires SUPER_ADMIN role"
- Suggest contacting system administrator

**B5: Real-Time Updates Paused**
- Manual refresh button available
- Auto-refresh toggle in settings
- Timestamp of last update displayed

#### Notifications

**System Alert Triggered:**
- **Email (CRITICAL/HIGH):** "System Alert: {alert_type}. {details}. Action required."
- **In-app:** Push notification with link to admin dashboard
- **SMS (CRITICAL only):** "Skillsier System Alert: {brief_message}"

**Daily System Report:**
- **Email (scheduled):** "Daily System Health Report: {date}. {summary}. [View Dashboard]"

**Anomaly Detected:**
- **In-app:** Toast: "Anomaly detected in {metric}. Review recommended."
- **Email:** "Unusual Activity Alert: {metric} {change_description}"

#### Analytics

- admin.dashboard.viewed (admin_id)
- admin.system_health.viewed (admin_id)
- admin.metrics.viewed (admin_id, metric_type)
- admin.metrics.drilldown (admin_id, metric_type, time_range)
- admin.alert.viewed (admin_id, alert_id)
- admin.alert.acknowledged (admin_id, alert_id)
- admin.alert.escalated (admin_id, alert_id, escalation_level)
- admin.incident.created (admin_id, alert_id, incident_id)
- admin.report.generated (admin_id, report_type, date_range)
- admin.dashboard.refresh (admin_id, auto_refresh_enabled)

#### Sources

**Backend:** admin-be.user-stories.md (system health, metrics, alerts), utility/analytics (metrics aggregation)  
**Frontend:** combined-fe-folder-structure.md ((dashboard)/admin routes, hooks/admin/use-system-health.ts, components/admin/system/)

### **ADM-2 — Content Moderation Queue**

**ID:** ADM-2  
**Persona:** Content Moderator, Moderation Manager  
**Preconditions:**
- User has MODERATOR or ADMIN role
- User authenticated and authorized
- Content moderation permissions granted

**Primary Screens:**

**Web:**
- `(dashboard)/admin/moderation` — Moderation dashboard
- `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/queue` — Moderation queue (pending items)
- `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/reports/[reportId]` — Report details
- `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/reports/[reportId]/review` — Review & take action
- `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/reports/resolved` — Resolved reports history

**Mobile:**
- `(dashboard)/admin/moderation` — Moderation dashboard (mobile-optimized)
- `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/queue` — Queue view (mobile)
- `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/reports/[reportId]` — Report detail (mobile)

**System Touchpoints:**
- **admin-be:** Moderation queue management, content review, actions
- **communications-be:** Message flagging, spam detection
- **reviews-be:** Review flagging, moderation state management
- **users-be:** User reporting, profile moderation
- **jobs-be:** Job posting moderation
- **proposals-be:** Proposal moderation

**Flow Steps:**

1. **Access Moderation Dashboard**
   - Moderator navigates to `(dashboard)/admin/moderation`
   - Dashboard displays:
     - Pending reports count by category
     - Today's actions summary (approved, rejected, escalated)
     - Average response time
     - Category breakdown (spam, harassment, inappropriate, fraud)
     - Quick navigation to queue

2. **View Moderation Queue**
   - Navigate to `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/queue`
   - Queue displays pending reports with:
     - Content type (message, review, job, proposal, profile)
     - Reporter information (masked for privacy)
     - Flag reason (spam, harassment, inappropriate, fraud, other)
     - Priority/severity (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, URGENT)
     - Auto-flag confidence score (if AI-flagged)
     - Timestamp (age of report)

3. **Filter & Sort Queue**
   - Apply filters:
     - Content type
     - Priority/severity
     - Flag reason
     - Date range
     - Auto-flagged vs user-reported
   - Sort options:
     - Priority (HIGH/URGENT first)
     - Oldest first
     - Newest first
     - Confidence score (for AI-flagged)

4. **Review Flagged Content**
   - Click on report to view details
   - System loads `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/reports/[reportId]`
   - Display shows:
     - Full content (with PII redaction if applicable)
     - Reporter information (anonymized if requested)
     - Reason for flag with details
     - Content author information
     - Content history & context
     - Previous moderation actions on author
     - AI confidence scores (if auto-flagged)
     - Evidence/screenshots (if provided)

5. **Take Moderation Action**
   - Navigate to `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/reports/[reportId]/review`
   - Moderator selects action:
     - **Approve**: Content is clean, dismiss flag
     - **Reject & Warn**: Issue warning to author, leave content
     - **Reject & Remove**: Remove content, issue warning
     - **Reject & Suspend**: Remove content, suspend author (1d, 7d, 30d, permanent)
     - **Escalate**: Send to senior moderator for review
   - Provide reason/notes (mandatory)
   - System validates action and applies it

6. **Confirm & Execute Action**
   - Review action summary
   - Click "Confirm Action"
   - System executes:
     - Updates content moderation state
     - Applies user penalty (if applicable)
     - Sends notification to content author
     - Sends notification to reporter (if requested)
     - Logs action in moderation history
     - Removes item from queue

7. **View Moderation History**
   - Navigate to `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/reports/resolved`
   - View resolved reports with filters:
     - Date range
     - Action taken
     - Moderator
     - Content type
   - Export history for compliance/audit

**Branches & Edge Cases:**

**B1: No Items in Queue**
- Show success message: "🎉 Great job! No pending reports at this time."
- Display summary of today's completed actions
- Quick link to resolved reports

**B2: High-Priority Items Aging**
- Show alert banner: "⚠️ {count} high-priority items are older than 2 hours. Review immediately."
- Auto-sort to show oldest high-priority first
- Escalation suggestion

**B3: Conflicting Reports on Same Content**
- Show indicator: "Multiple reports (x{count}) on this content"
- Display all report reasons
- Suggest: "Review all reports before taking action"

**B4: Content Already Removed/Modified**
- Show warning: "Content has been modified or removed since flag was created."
- Display original content (cached version)
- Options: "Dismiss flag" or "Take further action on author"

**B5: Insufficient Evidence**
- Moderator can request more information
- Options: "Request evidence from reporter" or "Escalate for investigation"
- Flag remains in queue with "PENDING_INFO" status

**B6: False Positive (Clean Content)**
- Moderator approves content
- System provides feedback to AI model (if auto-flagged)
- Reporter notified: "Report reviewed. Content meets guidelines."

**B7: Repeat Offender Detected**
- Show warning: "Author has {count} previous violations in last 30 days."
- Display moderation history
- Suggest escalated penalty

**B8: Escalation Required**
- For complex or sensitive cases
- Assign to senior moderator or compliance team
- Add escalation notes
- System notifies escalation target

**B9: Content in Multiple Languages**
- Detect language and provide translation option
- Show warning if content language doesn't match moderator's assigned languages
- Option to reassign to appropriate moderator

**B10: Large Batch of Similar Reports**
- Detect pattern (e.g., spam campaign)
- Suggest: "Bulk action available for similar reports"
- Option to apply action to all related reports

**B11: Appeal Submitted After Action**
- Show notification: "This action has been appealed."
- Link to appeal review process
- Action temporarily on hold (configurable)

**B12: Moderation Queue Overload**
- If queue size exceeds threshold (e.g., 500 items):
  - Show alert: "Queue capacity at {percentage}%. Consider auto-approve low-confidence items."
  - Suggest filters to focus on high-priority
  - Option to enable "Express Review" mode (simplified UI)

#### Notifications

**New Report in Queue:**
- **In-app (moderators):** "New moderation report: {content_type}. Priority: {priority}."
- **Push (mobile moderators):** "Urgent: New HIGH-priority report requires review."

**Action Completed:**
- **To Author:** "Your {content_type} has been reviewed. [Details]. [Appeal if needed]."
- **To Reporter:** "Your report has been reviewed. Action taken: {action}."

**Escalation Assigned:**
- **Email (senior moderator):** "Moderation case escalated to you: [Report ID]. Review required."
- **In-app:** "You've been assigned an escalated case: {report_id}"

**Queue Approaching SLA:**
- **Email (moderation manager):** "Moderation queue SLA at risk: {count} items older than 4 hours."
- **In-app:** Alert banner in dashboard

**Weekly Moderation Summary:**
- **Email (moderators):** "Your moderation summary: {actions_taken} actions, {accuracy_rate}% accuracy."

**AI Model Feedback:**
- **In-app (data science team):** "Moderation feedback collected: {count} false positives/negatives this week."

#### Analytics

- moderation.ai_feedback.provided (moderator_id, report_id, feedback_type)

### **ADM-3 — User Management & Account Actions**

**ID:** ADM-3  
**Persona:** User Manager, Compliance Officer, Admin  
**Preconditions:**
- User has ADMIN or USER_MANAGER role
- User authenticated and authorized
- User management permissions granted

**Primary Screens:**

**Web:**
- `(dashboard)/admin/users` — User management dashboard
- `(dashboard)/admin/users/search` — Search users
- `(dashboard)/admin/users/[userId]` — User profile & actions
- `(dashboard)/admin/users/[userId]/history` — User moderation history
- `(dashboard)/admin/users/flagged` — Flagged users list
- `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/users/[userId]` — User moderation actions

**Mobile:**
- `(dashboard)/admin/users` — User management (mobile-optimized)
- `(dashboard)/admin/users/[userId]` — User detail (mobile)

**System Touchpoints:**
- **admin-be:** User management, account actions, moderation
- **users-be:** User profile data, account status
- **contracts-be:** User contracts (for suspension impact)
- **financial-be:** User financial data (for compliance)
- **communications-be:** Notifications to users

**Flow Steps:**

1. **Access User Management Dashboard**
   - Admin navigates to `(dashboard)/admin/users`
   - Dashboard displays:
     - Total users (active, suspended, banned)
     - Recent account actions
     - Flagged users count
     - User growth trends (daily, weekly, monthly)
     - Search & filter options

2. **Search for User**
   - Navigate to `(dashboard)/admin/users/search`
   - Search options:
     - Email address
     - User ID
     - Name
     - Username
     - Phone number
     - IP address (last known)
   - System returns matching users

3. **View User Profile**
   - Click on user to load `(dashboard)/admin/users/[userId]`
   - Display user information:
     - **Profile:** Name, email, phone, avatar, bio
     - **Account Status:** Active, Suspended, Banned, Verification status
     - **Roles:** Freelancer, Client, Admin (if applicable)
     - **Registration:** Date, IP, referral source
     - **Activity:** Last login, activity level, engagement score
     - **Stats:** Jobs posted/applied, contracts, reviews, earnings/spending
     - **Risk Indicators:** Flags, reports, previous violations

4. **Review Moderation History**
   - Navigate to `(dashboard)/admin/users/[userId]/history`
   - Display:
     - Previous warnings issued
     - Suspensions (with dates, durations, reasons)
     - Bans (with dates, reasons, appeal status)
     - Content removals
     - Verification changes
     - All actions taken by moderators
   - Timeline view with full audit trail

5. **Take User Action**
   - Navigate to `(dashboard)/admin/moderation/users/[userId]`
   - Select action:
     - **Warn**: Issue warning (doesn't affect account)
     - **Suspend**: Temporary suspension (1d, 7d, 30d, custom)
     - **Ban**: Permanent or long-term ban
     - **Verify**: Grant verification badge
     - **Remove Verification**: Remove verification status
     - **Flag for Review**: Add to flagged users list
     - **Reset Password**: Force password reset on next login
     - **Lock Account**: Prevent login until manual review
   - Provide mandatory reason/notes
   - Select affected content action:
     - Leave content visible
     - Hide content (can be restored)
     - Remove content (permanent)

6. **Confirm Action & Execute**
   - Review action summary with impact:
     - Account status change
     - Content visibility change
     - Contract impact (will contracts be paused/terminated?)
     - Financial impact (will payouts be held?)
   - Click "Confirm Action"
   - System executes:
     - Updates user account status
     - Applies content action
     - Pauses/terminates contracts (if applicable)
     - Holds financial transactions (if applicable)
     - Sends notification to user (email + in-app)
     - Logs action in moderation history

7. **Review Flagged Users**
   - Navigate to `(dashboard)/admin/users/flagged`
   - View users flagged for review:
     - Risk score (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL)
     - Recent violations count
     - Active contracts count
     - Financial activity
     - Flag reason
   - Sort by: Risk score, violation count, date flagged
   - Take action or dismiss flag

**Branches & Edge Cases:**

**B1: User Has Active Contracts**
- Show warning: "User has {count} active contracts. Suspension/ban will pause these contracts."
- Display list of affected contracts
- Confirm: "Are you sure you want to proceed?"
- Options: "Pause contracts" or "Terminate with refund"

**B2: User Has Pending Payouts**
- Show warning: "User has {count} pending payouts totaling ${amount}. Ban will hold these funds."
- Options:
  - "Hold payouts pending investigation"
  - "Process payouts before ban"
  - "Cancel and refund transactions"
- Requires COMPLIANCE role for hold/cancel

**B3: Repeat Offender**
- Show alert: "User has {count} previous violations in last {days} days."
- Suggest escalated action: "Consider longer suspension or permanent ban."
- Display violation history timeline

**B4: User Suspended Multiple Times**
- If user has 3+ suspensions:
  - Show warning: "User has history of repeated violations. Permanent ban recommended."
  - Auto-suggest: "Ban" as default action

**B5: Verification Status Conflict**
- If removing verification:
  - Show warning: "This user has completed {verification_count} verifications. Removal requires justification."
  - Require COMPLIANCE or ADMIN role
  - Mandatory reason with 100+ character minimum

**B6: User Appeals Suspension/Ban**
- After action taken, if user appeals:
  - Show notification: "User has appealed this action. Review required."
  - Link to appeal review interface
  - Action may be temporarily on hold

**B7: User Not Found**
- If search returns no results:
  - Show message: "No users found matching '{query}'. Try different search criteria."
  - Suggest: Check email spelling, try user ID, try partial name

**B8: Action Requires Higher Permissions**
- If user lacks permission (e.g., trying to ban without ADMIN role):
  - Show error: "You don't have permission to perform this action. Requires {role}."
  - Option: "Request escalation to {senior_role}"

**B9: Bulk User Action**
- If flagged users list shows pattern:
  - Show option: "Apply bulk action to {count} users with similar violations?"
  - Requires ADMIN role
  - Confirmation with review step

**B10: User Account Deletion Request (GDPR)**
- If user requested account deletion:
  - Show notice: "User has requested account deletion (GDPR/CCPA)."
  - 30-day processing window displayed
  - Cannot take moderation actions after deletion request (except fraud cases)

**B11: IP/Device Ban**
- For severe violations:
  - Option to "Ban IP address" or "Ban device ID"
  - Show warning: "This will affect all accounts from this IP/device."
  - Requires SUPER_ADMIN role

**B12: Reinstate Suspended/Banned User**
- Option to "Unsuspend" or "Unban" user
  - Requires ADMIN or COMPLIANCE role
  - Mandatory reason with justification
  - System restores account access
  - Sends notification: "Your account has been reinstated."

#### Notifications

**Warning Issued:**
- **Email:** "Warning: Your Skillsier account. {reason}. Further violations may result in suspension."
- **In-app:** Alert with warning details and link to guidelines

**Account Suspended:**
- **Email:** "Your Skillsier account has been suspended. {reason}. Duration: {duration}. [Appeal here]"
- **In-app:** Banner: "Account suspended. [Details] [Appeal]"

**Account Banned:**
- **Email:** "Your Skillsier account has been banned. {reason}. [Appeal here if eligible]"
- **In-app:** Full-screen message (if user tries to login)

**Verification Granted:**
- **Email:** "Congratulations! Your Skillsier account is now verified. [View badge]"
- **In-app:** Toast: "You've been verified! 🎉"

**Verification Removed:**
- **Email:** "Your verification status has been removed. {reason}. [Contact support]"
- **In-app:** Alert: "Verification badge removed."

**Appeal Status Update:**
- **Email:** "Your appeal has been reviewed. Status: {approved/denied}. {details}"
- **In-app:** Notification with appeal decision

**Account Reinstated:**
- **Email:** "Good news! Your Skillsier account has been reinstated. [Login now]"
- **In-app:** Welcome back message with updated guidelines

#### Analytics

- admin.users.dashboard.viewed (admin_id)
- admin.users.searched (admin_id, search_type, search_value)
- admin.users.profile.viewed (admin_id, user_id)
- admin.users.history.viewed (admin_id, user_id)
- admin.users.action_page.viewed (admin_id, user_id)
- admin.users.action.taken (admin_id, user_id, action_type, reason_category)
- admin.users.action.confirmed (admin_id, user_id, action_type, contracts_affected, financial_impact)
- admin.users.flagged.viewed (admin_id, filters[])
- admin.users.flag.dismissed (admin_id, user_id, dismiss_reason)
- admin.users.bulk_action.applied (admin_id, action_type, user_count)
- admin.users.appeal.reviewed (admin_id, user_id, appeal_decision)
- admin.users.reinstated (admin_id, user_id, reinstate_reason)
- admin.users.verification.granted (admin_id, user_id, verification_type)
- admin.users.verification.removed (admin_id, user_id, removal_reason)

#### Sources

**Backend:** admin-be.user-stories.md (user_management domain), users-be.user-stories.md (user profile, account status)  
**Frontend:** combined-fe-folder-structure.md ((dashboard)/admin/users routes, hooks/admin/use-user-management.ts, components/admin/users/)
