#### Edge Cases & Alternate Flows

**E1: No Notifications**  
- **Empty state:**  
  - Show illustration and message  
  - "You're all caught up! 🎉"  
  - "No notifications at the moment"  
  - Suggest actions: "Browse jobs", "Check messages"  
- **First-time user:**  
  - Show welcome message  
  - Explain notification types  
  - Link to notification settings  

**E2: Network Issues**  
- **WebSocket disconnected:**  
  - Show "Connecting..." status  
  - Retry connection with exponential backoff  
  - Fall back to polling (every 30 seconds)  
  - Show offline indicator in header  
- **Failed to load notifications:**  
  - Show error message: "Failed to load notifications"  
  - Provide "Retry" button  
  - Cache last successful load  
  - Show cached data with warning  
- **Failed to mark as read:**  
  - Queue action for retry  
  - Show optimistic UI (mark as read immediately)  
  - Retry when connection restored  
  - Revert UI if retry fails  

**E3: Notification Overflow**  
- **Too many unread (100+):**  
  - Show "99+" badge instead of exact count  
  - Suggest "Mark all as read"  
  - Prioritize high-priority notifications  
  - Group aggressively (lower threshold)  
- **Too many in one category:**  
  - Auto-group after 10 notifications  
  - Show summary: "15 new job matches"  
  - Allow expanding to see all  
- **Notification storm (spam):**  
  - Detect abnormal rate (50+ in 1 minute)  
  - Auto-mute category temporarily  
  - Show warning: "High notification volume detected"  
  - Suggest adjusting preferences  

**E4: Notification Permissions**  
- **Browser notification permission not granted:**  
  - Show prompt to enable  
  - Explain benefits  
  - Gracefully degrade to in-app only  
  - Don't show prompt repeatedly (once per session)  
- **Browser notification permission denied:**  
  - Show info banner: "Browser notifications are disabled"  
  - Provide instructions to re-enable in browser settings  
  - Link to help article  
  - Still show in-app notifications  
- **Push notification permission denied (mobile):**  
  - Similar to browser notifications  
  - Guide user to app settings  
  - Don't repeatedly ask  

**E5: Notification Content Issues**  
- **Missing actor information:**  
  - Show generic: "Someone sent you a message"  
  - Fetch user data in background  
  - Update notification when data loads  
- **Deleted target (message, job, contract):**  
  - Show: "This item is no longer available"  
  - Disable action buttons  
  - Allow dismissing notification  
  - Don't show error on click  
- **Notification body too long:**  
  - Truncate at 150 characters  
  - Add "..." ellipsis  
  - Show full content on click/expand  
- **Invalid action URL:**  
  - Disable action button  
  - Show: "This link is no longer valid"  
  - Log error for debugging  

**E6: Quiet Hours / Do Not Disturb**  
- **During quiet hours:**  
  - Mute notification sounds  
  - Hide notification toasts  
  - Still show badge count  
  - Still add to notification center  
  - Show "Quiet hours active" indicator  
- **Urgent notification during quiet hours:**  
  - Override quiet hours if "allow urgent" enabled  
  - Show toast with different color (orange)  
  - Play different sound (gentle)  
  - Label as "Urgent" in notification  
- **Manually enable DND:**  
  - User can manually enable/disable  
  - Toggle in notification dropdown  
  - Show "Do Not Disturb" icon in header  
  - Respect until manually disabled or scheduled end  

**E7: Notification Timing Issues**  
- **Notification arrives after user views content:**  
  - Auto-mark as read (deduplicate)  
  - Don't show toast if already seen  
  - Update badge count correctly  
- **Notification delayed (slow delivery):**  
  - Show accurate timestamp ("2 hours ago")  
  - Don't show as "new" if old  
  - Mark automatically if content already viewed  
- **Duplicate notifications:**  
  - Deduplicate by notification_id  
  - Deduplicate by group_key  
  - Show only latest instance  
  - Don't increment badge twice  

**E8: Notification Action Failures**  
- **Action requires authentication:**  
  - Check auth status before performing  
  - Redirect to login if expired  
  - Return to notification after login  
  - Preserve notification context  
- **Action requires permission:**  
  - Show error: "You don't have permission"  
  - Explain why (e.g., "Contract already approved")  
  - Suggest alternative action  
  - Update notification status  
- **Action API call fails:**  
  - Show error toast  
  - Keep notification unread  
  - Allow retry  
  - Log error for debugging  
- **Target page doesn't exist (404):**  
  - Show: "This page is no longer available"  
  - Offer to dismiss notification  
  - Suggest related actions  

**E9: Bulk Operations Issues**  
- **Mark all as read with many notifications (1000+):**  
  - Show loading indicator  
  - Process in batches (100 at a time)  
  - Show progress: "Marking 234 of 1000..."  
  - Allow canceling  
  - Handle partial failures gracefully  
- **Clear all notifications:**  
  - Require confirmation  
  - Warn about important notifications  
  - Process in background  
  - Allow undo (5 seconds)  
  - Show progress for large batches  

**E10: Mobile-Specific Issues**  
- **App in background:**  
  - Queue notifications  
  - Batch update badge count  
  - Show notification banner (OS-level)  
  - Sync when app returns to foreground  
- **Low battery mode:**  
  - Reduce notification polling frequency  
  - Disable real-time updates  
  - Rely on push notifications only  
  - Show warning: "Real-time updates paused"  
- **Poor connection:**  
  - Cache notifications locally  
  - Show cached data  
  - Sync when connection improves  
  - Show "Offline" indicator  
- **Deep link from push notification:**  
  - Parse notification data  
  - Navigate to correct screen  
  - Mark notification as read  
  - Handle app cold start vs. running  

**E11: Notification Preference Conflicts**  
- **Global notifications disabled but category enabled:**  
  - Respect global setting (disable all)  
  - Show warning in category settings  
  - Suggest enabling global notifications  
- **Quiet hours vs. urgent notification:**  
  - Follow quiet hours exceptions setting  
  - If "allow urgent" enabled, show urgent notifications  
  - If disabled, queue until quiet hours end  
- **Email disabled but email digest enabled:**  
  - Show warning: "Email notifications are disabled"  
  - Disable digest automatically  
  - Suggest enabling email notifications  

**E12: Notification Retention & Cleanup**  
- **Notifications older than retention period:**  
  - Auto-delete after retention period (default 30 days)  
  - Show warning before deletion  
  - Allow extending retention for important notifications  
  - Archive instead of hard delete  
- **Storage quota exceeded:**  
  - Auto-delete oldest read notifications  
  - Prioritize keeping unread and important  
  - Show warning: "Notification storage almost full"  
  - Suggest adjusting retention settings  

**E13: Cross-Device Synchronization**  
- **Read on one device:**  
  - Sync read status across devices  
  - WebSocket event pushes update  
  - Update badge counts on all devices  
  - Dismiss toast on all devices  
- **Multiple devices showing same notification:**  
  - Use notification_id for deduplication  
  - Mark as read on one device = read on all  
  - Dismiss on one device = dismissed on all  
- **Delayed sync:**  
  - Show "Syncing..." indicator  
  - Resolve conflicts (last-write-wins)  
  - Refresh badge count after sync  

---

#### Notifications

**In-App Notifications (Meta):**  
- Notifications are the core of this journey  
- System provides in-app notifications for:  
  - Messages, mentions, replies  
  - Contract actions, milestones  
  - Proposal submissions, responses  
  - Payments, transactions  
  - Job matches, invitations  
  - Reviews, feedback  
  - System announcements  

**Push Notifications:**  
- **Delivered via:**  
  - Web Push (VAPID protocol)  
  - Mobile Push (FCM for Android, APNS for iOS)  
- **Content:**  
  - Title: Notification title  
  - Body: Notification body (truncated)  
  - Icon: Avatar or category icon  
  - Badge: Unread count  
  - Actions: Up to 2 action buttons  
  - Data: Deep link URL  
- **Behavior:**  
  - Show when app in background  
  - Group by category (mobile OS-level)  
  - Clear when notification marked as read  
  - Respect quiet hours settings  

**Email Notifications:**  
- **Immediate (transactional):**  
  - High-priority notifications  
  - Payment confirmations  
  - Security alerts  
  - @Mentions  
- **Digest (batched):**  
  - Daily or weekly summary  
  - Job matches  
  - General updates  
  - Configurable schedule  
- **Email content:**  
  - Subject: Notification title  
  - Body: Full notification content  
  - Actions: Clickable buttons  
  - Unsubscribe link: Required  
  - Preference link: Manage settings  

**Notification Channels:**  
- **In-app:** Always enabled (unless globally disabled)  
- **Push:** Requires permission, respects OS settings  
- **Email:** Requires email verification, respects preferences  
- **SMS:** Optional, for critical notifications only  

---

#### Analytics Events

**Notification Delivery:**  
- `notification_created` — Notification generated  
  - Properties: user_id, type, category, priority, has_actions  
- `notification_delivered` — Notification sent to user  
  - Properties: notification_id, channel (in_app/push/email), delivery_time_ms  
- `notification_delivery_failed` — Delivery error  
  - Properties: notification_id, channel, error_type, retry_count  

**Notification Engagement:**  
- `notification_viewed` — User opened notification center  
  - Properties: user_id, view_duration_seconds, unread_count  
- `notification_read` — Notification marked as read  
  - Properties: notification_id, method (manual/auto/clicked), time_to_read_seconds  
- `notification_dismissed` — Notification dismissed  
  - Properties: notification_id, time_to_dismiss_seconds  
- `notification_action_performed` — User clicked action button  
  - Properties: notification_id, action_id, action_type, success  
- `notification_clicked` — User clicked notification  
  - Properties: notification_id, category, destination_url  

**Notification Management:**  
- `notifications_mark_all_read` — Bulk mark as read  
  - Properties: user_id, count, duration_ms  
- `notifications_cleared_all` — All notifications dismissed  
  - Properties: user_id, count  
- `notification_snoozed` — Notification snoozed  
  - Properties: notification_id, snooze_duration_minutes  
- `notification_group_expanded` — Grouped notification expanded  
  - Properties: group_id, notification_count  

**Notification Settings:**  
- `notification_preferences_updated` — Settings changed  
  - Properties: user_id, changes (array of changed settings), quiet_hours_enabled  
- `notification_category_toggled` — Category enabled/disabled  
  - Properties: user_id, category, enabled, channel  
- `quiet_hours_enabled` — DND activated  
  - Properties: user_id, start_time, end_time, manual_override  
- `notification_sound_changed` — Sound settings updated  
  - Properties: user_id, sound_enabled, sound_type, volume  

**Notification Quality Metrics:**  
- `notification_time_to_read` — Time from creation to read  
  - Properties: notification_id, category, time_to_read_seconds  
- `notification_engagement_rate` — Percentage of notifications clicked  
  - Properties: user_id, category, engagement_rate_percentage  
- `notification_dismiss_rate` — Percentage of notifications dismissed  
  - Properties: user_id, category, dismiss_rate_percentage  
- `notification_group_effectiveness` — Grouped vs. individual engagement  
  - Properties: group_id, notification_count, engagement_rate  

**Funnels:**  
- **Notification Engagement Funnel:**  
  1. Notification created  
  2. Notification delivered  
  3. Notification viewed (center opened)  
  4. Notification read  
  5. Action performed or destination clicked  
- **Notification Settings Funnel:**  
  1. Settings page opened  
  2. Preference changed  
  3. Settings saved  
  4. Preferences applied to new notifications

#### Accessibility

**Keyboard Navigation:**  
- **Notification center:**  
  - `Tab` — Navigate between notifications  
  - `Enter` — Open/click notification  
  - `Delete` — Dismiss notification  
  - `Space` — Toggle read status  
  - `r` — Mark all as read  
  - `Esc` — Close notification center  
- **Notification item:**  
  - `Tab` — Move through action buttons  
  - `Enter` — Activate focused button  
  - `m` — Mark as read  
  - `d` — Dismiss notification  
- **Settings page:**  
  - `Tab` — Navigate form fields  
  - `Space` — Toggle checkboxes  
  - `Arrow keys` — Adjust sliders  
  - `Enter` — Save changes  

**Screen Reader Support:**  
- **Notification bell:**  
  - Announce: "Notifications, 5 unread"  
  - Button label: "View notifications"  
  - Badge: "5 unread notifications"  
- **Notification item:**

- **Grouped notification:**  
  - Announce: "Notification group, 5 new messages in E-commerce Project Team"  
  - Expandable: "Expand to view all 5 messages"  
- **Notification toast:**  
  - ARIA live region: "polite"  
  - Announce: "New notification: Message from Sarah Johnson"  
  - Auto-dismiss: Don't interrupt user mid-sentence  
- **Settings page:**  
  - Form labels: Proper label associations  
  - Fieldsets: Group related settings  
  - Help text: Descriptive aria-describedby  

**ARIA Labels:**

**Visual Accessibility:**  
- **High contrast mode:**  
  - Unread indicator: Bold border + icon  
  - Category colors: High contrast variations  
  - Action buttons: Clear borders  
  - Badge: High contrast background  
- **Color indicators:**  
  - Unread: Blue dot + bold text (not color-only)  
  - High priority: Orange accent + icon  
  - Success: Green checkmark + text  
  - Error: Red X + text  
- **Focus indicators:**  
  - Notification items: 2px blue outline  
  - Action buttons: Solid border  
  - Bell icon: Clear focus ring  
- **Text sizing:**  
  - Notification text: Scales with browser zoom  
  - Minimum 14px font size  
  - Adequate line height (1.5)  

**Motion & Animation:**  
- **Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`:**  
  - Disable slide-in animations  
  - Use instant transitions  
  - No auto-scroll  
  - No pulsing badge animations  
- **Notification toast:**  
  - Fade in/out only (no slide)  
  - Longer display time (8 seconds vs. 5)  
  - No auto-dismiss if interacted with  
- **Badge updates:**  
  - Instant count update (no animation)  
  - No color transitions

#### Performance Targets

**Notification Delivery:**  
- WebSocket latency: < 100ms (real-time)  
- Push notification delivery: < 2 seconds  
- Email notification: < 5 seconds (queue)  
- Notification creation: < 200ms (API)  

**Notification Center Loading:**  
- Initial load: < 800ms (50 notifications)  
- Open dropdown: < 300ms (cached)  
- Pagination: < 400ms (next 50)  
- Badge count: < 100ms (cached)  
- Category filter: < 200ms (client-side)  

**Notification Actions:**  
- Mark as read: < 200ms (API call)  
- Dismiss: < 150ms (API call)  
- Mark all as read: < 1s (batch 100)  
- Perform action: < 500ms (depends on action)  
- Snooze: < 250ms  

**Settings & Preferences:**  
- Load settings: < 500ms  
- Save preferences: < 400ms  
- Test notification: < 1s (send + deliver)  

**Real-Time Updates:**  
- WebSocket connect: < 2s  
- WebSocket reconnect: < 5s (with backoff)  
- Badge update: < 50ms (local state)  
- Toast display: < 100ms (render)  

**Mobile Performance:**  
- Notification list scroll: 60fps (virtualized)  
- Swipe gestures: < 50ms response  
- Badge update: < 100ms  
- Deep link navigation: < 800ms  

**Caching Strategy:**  
- Notification list: 2 min cache, stale-while-revalidate  
- Badge count: 1 min cache, real-time updates override  
- Preferences: 10 min cache  
- User avatars: 1 hour cache  

**Optimization Techniques:**  
- Virtualized list for 100+ notifications  
- Debounce badge count updates (100ms)  
- Batch mark as read operations  
- WebSocket connection pooling  
- Lazy load notification images  
- Service worker for background sync

#### Security

**Authentication & Authorization:**  
- **View notifications:**  
  - Verify user is authenticated  
  - Return only notifications for current user  
  - No cross-user notification access  
- **Mark as read/dismiss:**  
  - Verify notification belongs to user  
  - Return 404 if not found (not 403)  
  - Log action in audit trail  
- **Notification preferences:**  
  - User can only modify own preferences  
  - Validate all input values  
  - Rate limit preference updates  
- **Notification actions:**  
  - Verify user has permission for action  
  - Validate action data  
  - Check target resource exists and is accessible  
  - Rate limit action executions  

**Input Validation:**  
- **Notification content:**  
  - Sanitize HTML/markdown in body  
  - Validate URL schemes (no javascript:)  
  - Limit title: 100 characters  
  - Limit body: 500 characters  
  - Validate icon URLs (whitelist domains)  
- **Preferences:**  
  - Validate time formats (HH:MM)  
  - Validate days of week (mon-sun)  
  - Validate retention days (1-365)  
  - Boolean flags: true/false only  
  - Enums: Validate against allowed values  
- **Action data:**  
  - Validate action_type enum  
  - Sanitize action_data (no scripts)  
  - Validate URLs (internal or whitelisted external)  

**Content Security:**  
- **Notification body:**  
  - Strip all script tags  
  - Sanitize HTML (whitelist tags only)  
  - Escape user-generated content  
  - PII detection: Redact sensitive data  
- **External images:**  
  - Proxy through CDN  
  - Validate image URLs  
  - Set referrer policy  
  - CSP headers: Restrict sources  
- **XSS prevention:**  
  - Escape all dynamic content  
  - Use React's JSX (auto-escaping)  
  - Validate all URLs  
  - No inline scripts in notifications  

**Rate Limiting:**  
- **View notifications:**  
  - 100 requests per minute per user  
- **Mark as read:**  
  - 200 requests per minute per user  
- **Create notification (internal API):**  
  - 1000 per minute per service  
  - 10,000 per hour per service  
- **Update preferences:**  
  - 10 requests per minute per user  
  - Prevent preference spam  
- **Test notification:**  
  - 5 requests per hour per user  
  - Prevent abuse  

**Data Protection:**  
- **Notification storage:**  
  - Encrypt sensitive data at rest  
  - PII fields: Additional encryption layer  
  - TLS 1.3 for transit  
- **Notification retention:**  
  - Auto-delete after retention period  
  - Soft delete: Keep for 7 days (recovery)  
  - Hard delete: After 37 days  
  - Audit logs: 1 year retention  
- **WebSocket security:**  
  - Authenticate connection with JWT  
  - Validate origin header  
  - Rate limit messages  
  - Auto-disconnect after 1 hour idle  
- **Push notification security:**  
  - VAPID for web push (signed)  
  - Device token encryption  
  - Validate FCM/APNS responses  
  - Revoke invalid device tokens  

**Privacy:**  
- **Notification content:**  
  - Don't expose sensitive data in titles  
  - Truncate preview in push notifications  
  - Respect user privacy settings  
  - Allow disabling specific categories  
- **Read receipts:**  
  - Only sender can see read status  
  - Aggregate stats only (no individual tracking)  
- **Notification history:**  
  - User can delete notification history  
  - Admin cannot view user notifications (privacy)  
  - Audit logs anonymized after 90 days  

**Audit Trail:**  
- **Logged events:**  
  - Notification created (type, recipient)  
  - Notification delivered (channel, timestamp)  
  - Notification read (user, timestamp)  
  - Notification dismissed (user, timestamp)  
  - Preferences updated (user, changes)  
  - Action performed (user, action type, success)  
- **Audit log includes:**  
  - User ID, timestamp, action  
  - Notification ID  
  - IP address, user agent  
  - Result (success/failure)  
  - Error message (if failed)  
- **Retention:**  
  - Audit logs: 1 year  
  - Anonymize after 90 days (GDPR)

### Journey: COM-5 (Email Notifications & Digests)

**ID:** COM-5  
**Persona:** All Users (Freelancers, Clients, Admins)  
**Description:** Comprehensive email notification system enabling users to receive and manage transactional emails, event notifications, marketing communications, and digest emails (daily/weekly summaries). Includes email templates (versioned, internationalized), email tracking (opens, clicks, bounces), unsubscribe management, email-to-conversation threading, preference management per category, digest scheduling, and reply-to-message functionality. Supports all platform events including authentication, contracts, proposals, payments, messages, reviews, jobs, and system announcements.  

**Preconditions & Triggers:**  
**Triggers:**  
- User signs up and email verification is required  
- User requests password reset  
- User receives new message in conversation  
- Proposal is submitted, accepted, or rejected  
- Contract is created, signed, or milestone completed  
- Payment is received, processed, or requires action  
- Job is posted matching user's skills  
- Review is received or submitted  
- User is invited to conversation or team  
- System announcement or maintenance notice  
- Scheduled digest time is reached (daily/weekly)  
- User subscribes to job alerts  
- Invoice is generated or payment overdue  
- Account security alert (new login, suspicious activity)  
- User clicks "Send test email" in settings  
- User changes email address (verification required)  

**Preconditions:**  
- User has valid email address on file  
- User has verified email address (for non-transactional emails)  
- Email address is not bounced/blacklisted  
- User has not unsubscribed from category  
- User has email notifications enabled for category  
- Email service is operational (SendGrid/SES/Postmark)  
- Email templates are available and compiled  
- User's account is active (not suspended)  
- Email quota not exceeded (rate limits)  

**Primary Screens:**  
**Web:**  
- `(dashboard)/settings/notifications/email/page.tsx` — Email notification preferences  
- `(dashboard)/settings/notifications/email/digests/page.tsx` — Digest settings  
- `(dashboard)/settings/notifications/email/categories/page.tsx` — Per-category settings  
- `(dashboard)/settings/notifications/email/unsubscribe/page.tsx` — Unsubscribe management  
- `(dashboard)/settings/notifications/email/history/page.tsx` — Email delivery history  
- `(marketing)/unsubscribe/[token]/page.tsx` — Public unsubscribe page  
- `(marketing)/email-preferences/[token]/page.tsx` — Public preferences page  
- `(dashboard)/settings/account/email/page.tsx` — Change email address  

**Mobile:**  
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/notifications/email/index.tsx` — Email preferences  
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/notifications/email/digests.tsx` — Digest settings  
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/notifications/email/categories.tsx` — Category preferences  
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/notifications/email/history.tsx` — Delivery history  
- Native email client (for reading emails, not in-app)  

**System Touchpoints:**  
- **communications-be:**  
  - `email_notification/entity.go` — Email notification entity  
  - `email_template/entity.go` — Template management  
  - `email_preference/entity.go` — User email preferences  
  - `email_delivery/entity.go` — Delivery tracking  
  - `email_bounce/entity.go` — Bounce handling  
  - `email_digest/entity.go` — Digest generation  
  - `email_unsubscribe/entity.go` — Unsubscribe tokens  
  - `POST /v1/emails/send` — Send email (internal)  
  - `POST /v1/emails/send-bulk` — Bulk email sending  
  - `GET /v1/emails/preferences` — Get user preferences  
  - `PUT /v1/emails/preferences` — Update preferences  
  - `POST /v1/emails/preferences/category` — Update category preference  
  - `GET /v1/emails/templates` — List templates  
  - `GET /v1/emails/templates/{id}` — Get template  
  - `POST /v1/emails/test` — Send test email  
  - `GET /v1/emails/delivery-history` — Get delivery history  
  - `POST /v1/emails/unsubscribe` — Unsubscribe from category  
  - `POST /v1/emails/resubscribe` — Resubscribe  
  - `POST /v1/emails/unsubscribe-all` — Global unsubscribe  
  - `GET /v1/emails/unsubscribe/{token}` — Validate unsubscribe token  
  - `POST /v1/emails/digests/schedule` — Schedule digest  
  - `GET /v1/emails/digests/preview` — Preview digest content  
  - `POST /v1/emails/bounces/handle` — Handle bounce notification  
  - `POST /v1/emails/clicks/track` — Track email clicks  
  - `POST /v1/emails/opens/track` — Track email opens  
- **users-be:**  
  - `GET /v1/users/{id}` — Get user email address  
  - `PUT /v1/users/{id}/email` — Update email address  
  - `POST /v1/users/{id}/email/verify` — Send verification email  
  - `POST /v1/users/{id}/email/verify-token` — Verify email token  
- **All backend services:**  
  - Publish events that trigger email notifications  
- **External Email Service Provider (SendGrid/SES/Postmark):**  
  - `POST /v3/mail/send` — SendGrid API  
  - Webhook callbacks for opens, clicks, bounces, spam reports  
- **Events:**  
  - Subscribe to: `user.registered.v1`, `user.password-reset.v1`, `message.sent.v1`, `proposal.submitted.v1`, `contract.signed.v1`, `payment.completed.v1`, `review.received.v1`, `job.posted.v1`, `system.announcement.v1`, `digest.scheduled.v1`  
  - Publish: `email.sent.v1`, `email.delivered.v1`, `email.opened.v1`, `email.clicked.v1`, `email.bounced.v1`, `email.unsubscribed.v1`, `digest.sent.v1`

#### Flow Steps (Happy Path)

**A1: Send Transactional Email (Email Verification)**  
1. User registers new account  
2. Backend users-be creates user record with unverified email  
3. Backend publishes `user.registered.v1` event:  
```json
{
  "event_type": "user.registered",
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "email": "john.doe@example.com",
  "registration_timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z"
}
```
4. Email service (communications-be) receives event  
5. Check user email preferences:  
   - Transactional emails always sent (cannot be disabled)  
   - Verify email is not bounced  
6. Load email template: `email-verification.v1`  
7. Render template with variables:  
```json
{
  "user_name": "John Doe",
  "verification_link": "https://skillsier.com/auth/verify-email?token=abc123xyz",
  "verification_code": "ABC123",
  "expiry_hours": 24
}
```
8. Create email notification entity:  
```json
{
  "email_id": "email_abc123",
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "recipient_email": "john.doe@example.com",
  "category": "transactional",
  "subcategory": "email_verification",
  "template_id": "email-verification.v1",
  "template_version": "2.1",
  "subject": "Verify your Skillsier email address",
  "from_email": "noreply@skillsier.com",
  "from_name": "Skillsier",
  "reply_to": null,
  "priority": "high",
  "tracking_enabled": true,
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:00:01Z",
  "sent_at": null,
  "delivered_at": null,
  "opened_at": null,
  "clicked_at": null,
  "bounced_at": null,
  "metadata": {
    "verification_token": "abc123xyz",
    "user_locale": "en-US"
  }
}
```
9. Send email via email provider:  
   - Call SendGrid/SES API with rendered HTML  
   - Include tracking pixel for opens  
   - Include click tracking for links  
   - Set custom headers (X-Skillsier-Email-ID: email_abc123)  
10. Email provider returns success:  
```json
{
  "message_id": "sg_msg_456",
  "status": "queued",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:00:02Z"
}
```
11. Update email entity:  
   - Set sent_at = current timestamp  
   - Set provider_message_id = sg_msg_456  
   - Set status = "sent"  
12. Publish `email.sent.v1` event  
13. User receives email in inbox (typically within 1-5 seconds)  

**Email Template (Verification):**
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          [Skillsier Logo]                      │
│                                                                │
│ Hi John Doe,                                                   │
│                                                                │
│ Welcome to Skillsier! Please verify your email address to     │
│ activate your account and start connecting with clients or    │
│ freelancers.                                                   │
│                                                                │
│                   ┌──────────────────────┐                    │
│                   │ [Verify Email]       │                    │
│                   └──────────────────────┘                    │
│                                                                │
│ Or enter this verification code: ABC123                       │
```

**A2: Send Event Notification Email (New Message)**  
1. User receives new message in conversation  
2. Backend communications-be publishes `message.sent.v1` event  
3. Email service receives event  
4. Check if email notification should be sent:  
   - Is user online? (if yes, skip email, show in-app only)  
   - Check last email sent to user (rate limiting)  
   - Check user email preferences for "messages" category  
   - Check if user has unsubscribed from messages  
   - Check if within quiet hours  
5. If all checks pass, proceed to send email  
6. Load email template: `new-message.v1`  
7. Fetch conversation details:  
   - Call: `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}`  
   - Call: `GET /v1/messages/{message_id}`  
8. Render template with variables:  
```json
{
  "recipient_name": "Sarah Johnson",
  "sender_name": "Mike Chen",
  "sender_avatar_url": "https://cdn.skillsier.com/avatars/mike.jpg",

  "conversation_title": "E-commerce Website Project",
  "conversation_url": "https://skillsier.com/messages/conv_789",
  "reply_to_email": "reply+conv_789_msg_456@reply.skillsier.com",
  "unsubscribe_url": "https://skillsier.com/unsubscribe/token_xyz"
}
```
9. Create email notification entity with category = "messages"  
10. Send email with special reply-to address:

   - Reply-To: `reply+conv_789_msg_456@reply.skillsier.com`  
   - Subject: "New message from Mike Chen"

**A3: Email Tracking (Opens and Clicks)**  
1. User opens email in their email client  
2. Email client loads tracking pixel (1x1 transparent image):  
   - URL: `https://track.skillsier.com/email/email_abc123/open.gif`  
3. Tracking service receives GET request:  
   - Extract email_id from URL  
   - Record user_agent, IP address, timestamp  
4. Backend updates email entity:  
   - Set opened_at = first open timestamp  
   - Increment open_count  
   - Record open events (for multiple opens)  
5. Publish `email.opened.v1` event  
6. When user clicks link in email:  
   - Redirect through tracking URL:  
     - `https://track.skillsier.com/email/email_abc123/click?url=https://skillsier.com/messages/conv_789`  
7. Tracking service records click:  
   - Extract email_id, target URL  
   - Record user_agent, IP address, timestamp  
8. Backend updates email entity:  
   - Set clicked_at = first click timestamp  
   - Increment click_count  
   - Record clicked URLs  
9. Publish `email.clicked.v1` event  
10. Redirect user to target URL  

**A4: Generate and Send Digest Email (Daily Summary)**

2. For each user with digest enabled:

   - Check user timezone  
   - Calculate digest period (last 24 hours)  
3. Query for digest content:  
   - Call: `GET /v1/notifications?since=yesterday&user_id=user_123`  
   - Call: `GET /v1/messages/unread-count?user_id=user_123`  
   - Call: `GET /v1/contracts/pending-actions?user_id=user_123`  
   - Call: `GET /v1/jobs/recommendations?user_id=user_123&limit=3`

**A7: Handle Email Bounces**  
1. Email provider (SendGrid/SES) detects bounce  
2. Email provider sends webhook to: `POST /v1/emails/bounces/handle`  
```json
{
  "event_type": "bounce",
  "email": "invalid@example.com",
  "bounce_type": "hard",
  "reason": "Mailbox does not exist",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T16:00:00Z",
  "message_id": "sg_msg_456",
  "email_id": "email_abc123"
}
```
3. Backend processes bounce:  
   - Update email entity: Set bounced_at  
   - Set bounce_type: "hard" or "soft"  
   - Increment bounce count  
4. If hard bounce:  
   - Mark email address as invalid  
   - Disable email notifications for user  
   - Set flag: email_bounced = true  
   - Send in-app notification to user: "Email address invalid"  
5. If soft bounce (temporary):  
   - Retry after delay (exponential backoff)  
   - If 3 consecutive soft bounces → treat as hard bounce  
6. Publish `email.bounced.v1` event  
7. For users with bounced emails:  
   - Display banner in dashboard: "Please update your email address"  
   - Force email update before certain actions  

**A8: Send Test Email**  
1. User navigates to email settings  
2. User clicks "Send Test Email" button  
3. Call: `POST /v1/emails/test` with user_id  
4. Backend validates request:  
   - Check rate limit (5 per hour)  
   - Verify email address is valid (not bounced)  
5. Send test email immediately:  
   - Use template: `test-email.v1`  
   - Subject: "Test email from Skillsier"  
   - Body: Simple test message with timestamp  
6. Display success message: "Test email sent! Check your inbox."  
7. User receives test email within seconds

#### Edge Cases & Alternate Flows

**E1: Email Delivery Failure**  
- **Scenario:** Email provider API is down or returns error  
- **Handling:**  
  1. Catch error from email provider  
  2. Log error with full details  
  3. Mark email status as "failed"  
  4. Queue email for retry:  
     - Retry 1: After 1 minute  
     - Retry 2: After 5 minutes  
     - Retry 3: After 30 minutes  
  5. If all retries fail:  
     - Mark email as "permanently_failed"  
     - Send in-app notification: "Email delivery failed"  
     - Alert ops team (if critical email)  
  6. Don't retry for hard bounces (invalid email)  

**E2: User Email Address is Invalid/Bounced**  
- **Scenario:** User's email is marked as bounced  
- **Handling:**  
  1. Don't attempt to send email  
  2. Display warning banner in dashboard:  
     - "Your email address is invalid. Please update it."  
  3. Block certain actions until email updated:  
     - Contract signing  
     - Payment withdrawals  
  4. Send in-app notification with instructions  
  5. Allow user to update email in settings  
  6. After update, send verification email  
  7. Once verified, resume email notifications  

**E3: User Unverified Email Address**  
- **Scenario:** User registered but hasn't verified email  
- **Handling:**  
  1. Allow transactional emails only:  
     - Verification emails  
     - Password resets  
     - Security alerts  
  2. Block all other email notifications  
  3. Display banner: "Please verify your email to receive notifications"  
  4. Show "Resend Verification" button  
  5. After verification, enable all email categories based on preferences  

**E4: Email Rate Limiting Exceeded**  
- **Scenario:** User would receive too many emails in short time  
- **Handling:**  
  1. Apply rate limits per category:  
     - Messages: Max 1 email per 5 minutes per conversation  
     - Proposals: Max 3 emails per hour  
     - Payments: No limit (critical)  
  2. If rate limit exceeded:  
     - Queue notification for digest instead  
     - Don't send instant email  
     - Log rate limit hit  
  3. Show rate limit summary in next digest  
  4. For critical notifications (payments, security):  
     - Bypass rate limits  
     - Always send immediately  

**E5: User in Quiet Hours / Do Not Disturb**  
- **Scenario:** Email would be sent during user's quiet hours  
- **Handling:**  
  1. Check if current time is within quiet hours:  
     - Start: 22:00, End: 08:00 (user timezone)  
  2. If yes:  
     - Queue non-urgent emails for after quiet hours  
     - Add to pending digest  
  3. Send at end of quiet hours (8:00 AM):  
     - Send queued emails  
     - Or include in morning digest  
  4. Exceptions (always send immediately):  
     - Security alerts  
     - Payment received  
     - Contract signed  
     - Password reset  
     - Email verification  
  5. Display indicator in settings: "🔕 Quiet Hours Active"  

**E6: Email Content Personalization Error**  
- **Scenario:** Template variable is missing or invalid  
- **Handling:**  
  1. Template engine detects missing variable  
  2. Use fallback values:  
     - {{user_name}} → "there" or "user"  
     - {{sender_name}} → "A user"  
     - {{amount}} → "$0.00" (with warning)  
  3. Log template error with details  
  4. Continue sending email with fallbacks  
  5. Alert template team for investigation  
  6. Don't block email sending for minor issues  

**E7: User Changes Email Address**  
- **Scenario:** User updates email address in settings  
- **Handling:**  
  1. User enters new email address  
  2. Call: `PUT /v1/users/{id}/email` with new email  
  3. Backend validates new email:  
     - Check format (RFC 5322)  
     - Check not already used by another user  
     - Check not in bounce list  
  4. Create pending email change:  
     - Store new email in pending_email field  
     - Generate verification token  
  5. Send verification email to NEW address:  
     - "Verify your new email address"  
     - Include verification link  
  6. Send notification to OLD address:  
     - "Your email address change request"  
     - Include cancel link (in case of hack)  
  7. Old email remains active until verified  
  8. User clicks verification link in new email  
  9. Backend confirms change:  
     - Move pending_email → email  
     - Clear pending_email  
     - Mark new email as verified  
  10. Send confirmation to both addresses  
  11. Update all email preferences to use new address  

**E8: Digest Has No Content**  
- **Scenario:** Digest scheduled but user has no activity  
- **Handling:**  
  1. Generate digest content  
  2. Check if content exists:  
     - No unread messages  
     - No pending actions  
     - No new jobs  
     - No notifications  
  3. If empty:  
     - Don't send email (skip)  
     - Log: "Digest skipped - no content"  
     - Don't count against email quota  
  4. Mark digest as "skipped" in database  
  5. Next scheduled digest will run normally  

**E9: Email Reply to Conversation Fails**  
- **Scenario:** User replies to email but reply cannot be processed  
- **Handling:**  
  1. Inbound email processor receives reply  
  2. Parse reply-to address to extract conversation_id  
  3. If conversation not found:  
     - Reply to user: "Conversation not found"  
     - Include link to all conversations  
     - Don't create orphan message  
  4. If user not participant in conversation:  
     - Reply: "You're not part of this conversation"  
     - Don't add message  
  5. If conversation is archived/closed:  
     - Reply: "This conversation is closed"  
     - Offer to reopen or create new  
  6. If message parsing fails (too large, invalid format):  
     - Reply: "Unable to process your email"  
     - Suggest using platform directly  
  7. For all failures:  
     - Log error with email content  
     - Send friendly error response  
     - Provide alternative actions  

**E10: Spam/Abuse Report Received**  
- **Scenario:** User marks email as spam in email client  
- **Handling:**  
  1. Email provider sends spam report webhook  
  2. Backend receives spam complaint:  
```json
{
  "event_type": "spam_complaint",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T18:00:00Z",
  "email_id": "email_abc123"
}
```
  3. Immediately disable all emails to user:  
     - Set global_enabled = false  
     - Add to suppression list  
  4. Create spam complaint record  
  5. Send in-app notification:  
     - "We noticed you marked our email as spam"  
     - "We've disabled all emails. You can re-enable in settings."  
  6. Investigate spam complaint:  
     - Review email content  
     - Check if content was appropriate  
     - Adjust templates if needed  
  7. Allow user to re-enable in settings manually  
  8. Publish `email.spam-complaint.v1` event  

**E11: Email Template Not Found**  
- **Scenario:** Email service tries to load template that doesn't exist  
- **Handling:**  
  1. Template service can't find template_id  
  2. Check for fallback template:  
     - Try previous version (e.g., v2.0 → v1.9)  
     - Try default template for category  
  3. If no fallback available:  
     - Use generic plain-text template  
     - Include basic information only  
     - Log error with severity: HIGH  
  4. Alert template team immediately  
  5. Continue email sending (don't block)  
  6. For critical emails (verification, password reset):  
     - Use hardcoded fallback template  
     - Never fail  

**E12: User Requests GDPR Data Export (Email History)**  
- **Scenario:** User requests download of all email history  
- **Handling:**  
  1. User clicks "Export Email History" in settings  
  2. Call: `POST /v1/emails/export-request`  
  3. Backend creates async export job:  
```json
{
  "export_id": "export_123",
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "type": "email_history",
  "status": "processing",
  "requested_at": "2025-01-15T19:00:00Z"
}
```
  4. Background job gathers data:  
     - All sent emails (metadata)  
     - Email preferences history  
     - Bounce records  
     - Unsubscribe records  
     - Digest history  
  5. Generate export file:  
     - Format: JSON or CSV  
     - Include all email metadata  
     - Don't include full email HTML (PII concerns)  
  6. Upload export to secure storage  
  7. Send email with download link:  
     - Link expires in 7 days  
     - Download tracked  
  8. User downloads export  
  9. Auto-delete export after 7 days  

**E13: User Requests Email Deletion (Right to be Forgotten)**  
- **Scenario:** User requests deletion of all email data  
- **Handling:**  
  1. User submits deletion request  
  2. Backend initiates deletion process:  
     - Mark all emails as "to_be_deleted"  
     - Set deletion_scheduled_at = now + 30 days  
  3. During 30-day grace period:  
     - User can cancel deletion  
     - No new emails sent  
     - Display banner: "Account deletion pending"  
  4. After 30 days:  
     - Soft delete all email records  
     - Anonymize email addresses in audit logs  
     - Remove from email provider suppression lists  
     - Clear all email preferences  
  5. After 90 days:  
     - Hard delete all email data  
     - Remove from backups  
  6. Publish `email.data.deleted.v1` event

#### Accessibility

**Keyboard Navigation:**  
- Tab through email preference toggles  
- Enter/Space to toggle checkboxes  
- Tab through digest time selectors  
- Arrow keys in dropdown selectors  
- Esc to close modals/dropdowns  

**Screen Reader Support:**  
- Label all form inputs with aria-label  
- Announce preference changes: "Messages email enabled"  
- Announce validation errors: "Invalid email format"  
- Describe email frequency options clearly  
- Announce digest schedule changes  
- Label all action buttons descriptively  

**Visual Accessibility:**  
- High contrast for all text  
- Clear labels for all toggles  
- Large touch targets for mobile (44×44px)  
- Loading indicators for save operations  
- Success/error colors with icons (not color-only)  
- Email preview readable at all zoom levels  

**Email Accessibility:**  
- Semantic HTML in email templates  
- Alt text for all images  
- High contrast text (4.5:1 minimum)  
- Large font sizes (16px minimum for body)  
- Descriptive link text (not "click here")  
- Plain text alternative for all HTML emails  
- Table-based layouts for email client compatibility

#### Performance Targets

**Email Sending:**  
- Time to send transactional email: <2 seconds  
- Time to send bulk emails: <5 minutes per 10,000 emails  
- Email delivery rate: >99%  
- Bounce rate: <2%  
- Complaint rate: <0.1%  

**Template Rendering:**  
- Template compilation time: <50ms  
- Template rendering with data: <100ms  
- Cache compiled templates (in-memory)  
- Template loading from storage: <10ms  

**Email Tracking:**  
- Tracking pixel load time: <50ms  
- Click redirect time: <100ms  
- Tracking event processing: <200ms (async)  

**Digest Generation:**  
- Digest content aggregation: <2 seconds per user  
- Digest batch processing: 1000 users per minute  
- Digest HTML rendering: <100ms per digest  

**Email Preferences:**  
- Load preferences: <200ms  
- Save preferences: <500ms  
- Preference updates reflected immediately  

**Database Queries:**  
- Get user email preferences: <50ms  
- Get email delivery history: <100ms (paginated)  
- Get bounce status: <30ms (cached)  

**Webhook Processing:**  
- Process bounce webhook: <500ms  
- Process open/click webhook: <200ms  
- Process spam complaint: <1 second

#### Security

**Authentication & Authorization:**  
- **Email preferences:**  
  - User can only view/update own preferences  
  - JWT authentication required  
  - CSRF token for state-changing operations  
- **Unsubscribe tokens:**  
  - Signed with HMAC-SHA256  
  - Include user_id, category, expiry (90 days)  
  - Cannot be tampered with  
  - Verify signature before processing  
- **Email reply-to addresses:**  
  - Encode conversation_id + user_id + signature  
  - Verify signature before posting message  
  - Check user is participant in conversation  
  - Rate limit replies (10 per hour per user)  

**Input Validation:**  
- **Email addresses:**  
  - Validate format (RFC 5322 compliant)  
  - Max length: 254 characters  
  - Reject disposable email domains  
  - Check against DNS (MX records)  
  - Sanitize before storage  
- **Template variables:**  
  - Whitelist allowed variables  
  - Escape all user-generated content  
  - Sanitize HTML (strip scripts)  
  - Validate URLs (no javascript:)  
- **Preference values:**  
  - Validate enums (frequency, category)  
  - Validate time formats (HH:MM)  
  - Validate timezone (IANA database)  
  - Boolean values: true/false only  

**Content Security:**  
- **Email templates:**  
  - No inline JavaScript in templates  
  - Sanitize all dynamic content  
  - Escape HTML entities  
  - Validate image URLs (CDN only)  
  - CSP headers in HTML emails  
- **Email tracking:**  
  - Signed tracking URLs (prevent spoofing)  
  - HTTPS only for all links  
  - No PII in tracking URLs  
  - Rate limit tracking endpoints  
- **XSS Prevention:**  
  - Escape all user input in templates  
  - Use templating engine with auto-escaping  
  - Validate all URLs before rendering  
  - Sanitize email body on display  

**Rate Limiting:**  
- **Send email (internal API):**  
  - 10,000 emails per hour per service  
  - 100,000 emails per day per service  
- **User preference updates:**  
  - 10 requests per minute per user  
- **Test email:**  
  - 5 requests per hour per user  
- **Unsubscribe:**  
  - 10 requests per hour per IP  
- **Email replies:**  
  - 10 replies per hour per user  
  - 50 replies per day per user  
- **Digest generation:**  
  - 1 digest per user per configured interval  
  - Max 1 daily + 1 weekly per user  

**Data Protection:**  
- **Email storage:**  
  - Encrypt email addresses at rest (AES-256)  
  - Email content not stored (metadata only)  
  - Bounce records encrypted  
  - TLS 1.3 for transit  
- **Email provider credentials:**  
  - Store API keys in secrets manager  
  - Rotate keys every 90 days  
  - Use separate keys per environment  
  - Never log API keys  
- **Tracking data:**  
  - Anonymize IP addresses (mask last octet)  
  - Don't store full user agent  
  - Aggregate data after 90 days  
  - Delete detailed logs after 1 year  
- **PII Protection:**  
  - Email addresses hashed in logs  
  - Redact email content in error logs  
  - Anonymize bounce reasons (no email addresses)  
  - GDPR-compliant data retention  

**Privacy:**  
- **Email content:**  
  - Don't include sensitive data in subject lines  
  - Truncate previews to 50 characters  
  - Respect user privacy preferences  
  - Allow disabling all non-transactional emails  
- **Tracking opt-out:**  
  - Honor "Do Not Track" header  
  - Allow disabling open/click tracking  
  - Respect email client privacy features  
- **Third-party sharing:**  
  - Never share email addresses with third parties  
  - Email provider bound by DPA  
  - No marketing data sold  
- **Unsubscribe:**  
  - One-click unsubscribe (List-Unsubscribe header)  
  - No login required to unsubscribe  
  - Immediate processing (no delays)  
  - Confirmation not required  

**Compliance:**  
- **CAN-SPAM Act:**  
  - Include physical address in footer  
  - Honor opt-out requests within 10 days  
  - Identify email as advertisement (if marketing)  
  - Accurate "From" and "Subject" headers  
- **GDPR:**  
  - Explicit consent for marketing emails  
  - Easy unsubscribe mechanism  
  - Right to access email history  
  - Right to deletion (30-day grace period)  
  - Data retention policies enforced  
- **CASL (Canada):**  
  - Implied consent for transactional  
  - Express consent for commercial  
  - Unsubscribe in every email  
  - Contact information in footer  

**Audit Trail:**  
- **Logged events:**  
  - Email sent (recipient, category, template)  
  - Email delivered/bounced (status, reason)  
  - Email opened/clicked (timestamp, count)  
  - Preferences updated (user, changes)  
  - Unsubscribed (user, category, source)  
  - Spam complaint (email_id, user)  
  - Email address changed (user, verification status)  
- **Audit log includes:**  
  - User ID (hashed)  
  - Timestamp, action  
  - Email ID reference  
  - IP address (anonymized)  
  - Result (success/failure)  
  - Error message (if failed)  
- **Retention:**  
  - Audit logs: 1 year  
  - Anonymize after 90 days  
  - Email metadata: Per retention policy  
  - Bounce records: 2 years

### Journey: COM-6 (Push Notifications (Web & Mobile))

**ID:** COM-6  
**Persona:** All Users (Freelancers, Clients, Admins)  
**Description:** Comprehensive push notification system enabling users to receive real-time push notifications on web (via Web Push API/VAPID) and mobile (via APNS for iOS, FCM for Android). Includes device token registration and management, push notification delivery, rich push notifications with images/actions, notification grouping/stacking, push permission management, notification channels/categories, badge count management, sound/vibration customization, notification action handling, foreground/background delivery, and unsubscribe management per device.  

**Preconditions & Triggers:**  
**Triggers:**  
- User grants push notification permission in browser/app  
- User receives new message in conversation  
- Proposal is submitted, accepted, or rejected  
- Contract milestone is completed or requires action  
- Payment is received or processed  
- Job is posted matching user's skills  
- Review is received or submitted  
- User is @mentioned in message or thread  
- System announcement or security alert  
- Contract deadline approaching  
- User installs mobile app first time  
- User logs in on new device  
- User navigates to notification settings  
- Scheduled reminder is due  

**Preconditions:**  
- User has granted push notification permission  
- User's device/browser supports push notifications  
- Device token is registered with backend  
- Push notification service is operational (FCM/APNS)  
- User has push notifications enabled for category  
- User is authenticated  
- Device has internet connection  
- For web: HTTPS connection (required for Web Push)  
- For mobile: App has proper certificates/keys configured  
- User's device is not in Do Not Disturb mode (or notification is critical)  

**Primary Screens:**  
**Web:**  
- `(dashboard)/settings/notifications/push/page.tsx` — Push notification settings  
- `(dashboard)/settings/notifications/push/devices/page.tsx` — Manage devices  
- `components/push/permission-prompt/` — Permission request UI  
- `components/push/notification-preview/` — Browser notification preview  
- Service Worker: `public/sw.js` — Background push handling  

**Mobile:**  
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/notifications/push/index.tsx` — Push settings  
- `(mobile)/(app)/settings/notifications/push/devices.tsx` — Device management  
- `components/push/permission-prompt/` — Native permission request  
- Native notification handling (iOS/Android)  
- App Delegate / MainActivity — Push setup  

**System Touchpoints:**  
- **communications-be:**  
  - `push_notification/entity.go` — Push notification entity  
  - `push_device/entity.go` — Device token management  
  - `push_subscription/entity.go` — Web push subscriptions  
  - `push_preference/entity.go` — User push preferences  
  - `push_delivery/entity.go` — Delivery tracking  
  - `POST /v1/push/send` — Send push notification (internal)  
  - `POST /v1/push/send-bulk` — Bulk push sending  
  - `POST /v1/push/devices/register` — Register device token  
  - `DELETE /v1/push/devices/{deviceId}` — Unregister device  
  - `GET /v1/push/devices` — List user devices  
  - `PUT /v1/push/devices/{deviceId}` — Update device info  
  - `GET /v1/push/preferences` — Get push preferences  
  - `PUT /v1/push/preferences` — Update preferences  
  - `POST /v1/push/preferences/category` — Update category preference  
  - `POST /v1/push/test` — Send test push notification  
  - `POST /v1/push/vapid/subscribe` — Subscribe to Web Push (VAPID)  
  - `DELETE /v1/push/vapid/unsubscribe` — Unsubscribe from Web Push  
  - `GET /v1/push/vapid/public-key` — Get VAPID public key  
  - `POST /v1/push/delivery-report` — Report delivery status  
  - `POST /v1/push/action` — Handle notification action  
- **users-be:**  
  - `GET /v1/users/{id}` — Get user info  
  - `GET /v1/users/{id}/devices` — Get user's registered devices  
- **All backend services:**  
  - Publish events that trigger push notifications  
- **External Push Services:**  
  - **Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM):**  
    - `POST https://fcm.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/messages:send`  
    - Push to Android devices  
  - **Apple Push Notification Service (APNS):**  
    - `POST https://api.push.apple.com/3/device/{deviceToken}`  
    - Push to iOS devices  
  - **Web Push Protocol (VAPID):**  
    - Direct push to browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari)  
- **Events:**  
  - Subscribe to: `message.sent.v1`, `proposal.submitted.v1`, `contract.signed.v1`, `payment.completed.v1`, `review.received.v1`, `job.posted.v1`, `mention.created.v1`, `system.announcement.v1`  
  - Publish: `push.sent.v1`, `push.delivered.v1`, `push.clicked.v1`, `push.dismissed.v1`, `push.failed.v1`, `device.registered.v1`, `device.unregistered.v1`  

---

#### Flow Steps (Happy Path)

**A1: Request Push Notification Permission (Web)**  
1. User visits Skillsier web app (first time or after clearing data)  
2. Frontend checks current permission status:  
```javascript
const permission = Notification.permission;
// Values: "default", "granted", "denied"
```
3. If permission is "default" (not yet asked):  
   - Wait for appropriate moment (after user engagement)  
   - Show custom permission prompt (friendlier than browser default):  

**Web Permission Prompt:**
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                │
│                         🔔                                     │
│                                                                │
│         Stay Updated with Push Notifications                  │
│                                                                │
│    Get real-time alerts for:                                  │
│    • New messages from clients and freelancers                │
│    • Proposal updates and contract milestones                 │
│    • Payment notifications                                    │
│    • Job opportunities matching your skills                   │
│                                                                │
│    You can change this anytime in settings.                   │
│                                                                │
│         [Enable Notifications]    [Maybe Later]               │
│                                                                │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

4. User clicks "Enable Notifications"  
5. Frontend requests browser permission:  
```javascript
const permission = await Notification.requestPermission();
```
6. Browser shows native permission dialog  
7. User clicks "Allow" in browser dialog  
8. Permission granted: `permission === "granted"`  
9. Register service worker (if not already registered):  
```javascript
const registration = await navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js');
await navigator.serviceWorker.ready;
```
10. Subscribe to push notifications (VAPID):  
```javascript
const subscription = await registration.pushManager.subscribe({
  userVisibleOnly: true,
  applicationServerKey: vapidPublicKey // Get from backend
});
```
11. Subscription object contains:  
```json
{
  "endpoint": "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/abc123...",
  "keys": {
    "p256dh": "base64-encoded-key",
    "auth": "base64-encoded-auth"
  }
}
```
12. Send subscription to backend:  
    - Call: `POST /v1/push/vapid/subscribe`  
```json
{
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "subscription": {
    "endpoint": "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/abc123...",
    "keys": {
      "p256dh": "...",
      "auth": "..."
    }
  },
  "device_info": {
    "browser": "Chrome",
    "browser_version": "120.0",
    "os": "Windows",
    "os_version": "11"
  }
}
```
13. Backend saves subscription:  
    - Create push_subscription entity  
    - Store endpoint and keys (encrypted)  
    - Associate with user_id  
14. Backend returns success  
15. Frontend shows success message: "Push notifications enabled! ✅"  
16. Publish `device.registered.v1` event  

**A2: Request Push Notification Permission (Mobile iOS)**  
1. User opens Skillsier mobile app (first launch)  
2. App checks notification permission status:  
```swift
let center = UNUserNotificationCenter.current()
let settings = await center.notificationSettings()
// authorizationStatus: .notDetermined, .authorized, .denied
```
3. If status is `.notDetermined`:  
   - Show custom onboarding screen explaining benefits  
   - Display at appropriate time (after profile setup)  

**Mobile Permission Screen:**
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                        │
│              🔔                        │
│                                        │
│     Enable Notifications               │
│                                        │
│ Get instant alerts for:                │
│                                        │
│ 💬 New messages                        │
│ 📋 Proposal updates                    │
│ 💰 Payments received                   │
│ 🎯 Matching job opportunities          │
│                                        │
│ You can customize notification         │
│ preferences anytime in Settings.       │
│                                        │
│                                        │
│    [Enable Notifications]              │
│                                        │
│         [Not Now]                      │
│                                        │
└────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

4. User taps "Enable Notifications"  
5. Request iOS notification permission:  
```swift
let options: UNAuthorizationOptions = [.alert, .sound, .badge]
let granted = try await center.requestAuthorization(options: options)
```
6. iOS shows system permission dialog  
7. User taps "Allow"  
8. Permission granted: `granted == true`  
9. Register for remote notifications:  
```swift
await UIApplication.shared.registerForRemoteNotifications()
```
10. App receives device token in delegate method:  
```swift
func application(_ application: UIApplication, 
                 didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken deviceToken: Data) {
    let token = deviceToken.map { String(format: "%02.2hhx", $0) }.joined()
    // token: "abc123def456..."
}
```
11. Send device token to backend:  
    - Call: `POST /v1/push/devices/register`  
```json
{
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "device_token": "abc123def456...",
  "platform": "ios",
  "device_info": {
    "device_model": "iPhone 14 Pro",
    "os_version": "17.2",
    "app_version": "2.1.0",
    "device_name": "Sarah's iPhone"
  }
}
```
12. Backend saves device:  
```json
{
  "device_id": "device_abc123",
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "device_token": "abc123def456...",
  "platform": "ios",
  "device_model": "iPhone 14 Pro",
  "os_version": "17.2",
  "app_version": "2.1.0",
  "device_name": "Sarah's iPhone",
  "registered_at": "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z",
  "last_active_at": "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z",
  "status": "active"
}
```
13. Backend returns success with device_id  
14. App stores device_id locally  
15. Show success message in app  
16. Publish `device.registered.v1` event  

**A3: Request Push Notification Permission (Mobile Android)**  
1. User opens Skillsier mobile app (first launch)  
2. Check if running Android 13+ (requires runtime permission):  
```kotlin
if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
    // Android 13+ requires POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission
}
```
3. Show custom permission explanation screen (similar to iOS)  
4. User taps "Enable Notifications"  
5. For Android 13+, request runtime permission:  
```kotlin
requestPermissions(arrayOf(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS))
```
6. Android shows system permission dialog  
7. User taps "Allow"  
8. Get FCM token:  
```kotlin
FirebaseMessaging.getInstance().token.addOnCompleteListener { task ->
    if (task.isSuccessful) {
        val token = task.result // FCM token
    }
}
```
9. FCM token received: "fcm_token_xyz789..."  
10. Send FCM token to backend:  
    - Call: `POST /v1/push/devices/register`  
```json
{
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "device_token": "fcm_token_xyz789...",
  "platform": "android",
  "device_info": {
    "device_model": "Samsung Galaxy S23",
    "os_version": "14",
    "app_version": "2.1.0",
    "device_name": "Sarah's Phone"
  }
}
```
11. Backend saves device (same structure as iOS)  
12. Backend returns success  
13. App stores device_id locally  
14. Show success message  
15. Publish `device.registered.v1` event  

**A4: Send Push Notification (Backend)**  
1. Backend event occurs (e.g., new message sent)  
2. Notification service processes event:  
   - Determine notification recipients  
   - Check user push preferences  
   - Check if user is online (skip if active in app)  
   - Get user's registered devices  
3. Load user devices:  
   - Call: `GET /v1/push/devices?user_id=user_123&status=active`  
4. Backend returns devices:  
```json
{
  "devices": [
    {
      "device_id": "device_abc123",
      "platform": "ios",
      "device_token": "abc123def456...",
      "device_name": "Sarah's iPhone"
    },
    {
      "device_id": "device_xyz789",
      "platform": "android",
      "device_token": "fcm_token_xyz789...",
      "device_name": "Sarah's Tablet"
    },
    {
      "device_id": "device_web123",
      "platform": "web",
      "subscription": {
        "endpoint": "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/...",
        "keys": { "p256dh": "...", "auth": "..." }
      },
      "device_name": "Chrome on Windows"
    }
  ]
}
```
5. For each device, create push notification payload:  

**iOS (APNS) Payload:**
```json
{
  "aps": {
    "alert": {
      "title": "New message from Mike Chen",
      "body": "I've reviewed the designs and they look great!",
      "subtitle": "E-commerce Website Project"
    },
    "badge": 5,
    "sound": "default",
    "category": "message",
    "thread-id": "conv_789",
    "mutable-content": 1
  },
  "data": {
    "notification_id": "notif_abc123",
    "type": "message",
    "conversation_id": "conv_789",
    "message_id": "msg_456",
    "sender_id": "user_456",
    "sender_name": "Mike Chen",
    "sender_avatar": "https://cdn.skillsier.com/avatars/mike.jpg",
    "action_url": "skillsier://messages/conv_789"
  }
}
```

**Android (FCM) Payload:**
```json
{
  "message": {
    "token": "fcm_token_xyz789...",
    "notification": {
      "title": "New message from Mike Chen",
      "body": "I've reviewed the designs and they look great!",
      "image": "https://cdn.skillsier.com/avatars/mike.jpg"
    },
    "android": {
      "priority": "high",
      "notification": {
        "channel_id": "messages",
        "icon": "ic_notification",
        "color": "#FF6B35",
        "sound": "default",
        "tag": "conv_789",
        "click_action": "OPEN_CONVERSATION"
      }
    },
    "data": {
      "notification_id": "notif_abc123",
      "type": "message",
      "conversation_id": "conv_789",
      "message_id": "msg_456",
      "sender_id": "user_456",
      "sender_name": "Mike Chen",
      "action_url": "skillsier://messages/conv_789"
    }
  }
}
```

**Web Push (VAPID) Payload:**
```json
{
  "notification": {
    "title": "New message from Mike Chen",
    "body": "I've reviewed the designs and they look great!",
    "icon": "https://cdn.skillsier.com/avatars/mike.jpg",
    "badge": "https://skillsier.com/images/badge-icon.png",
    "tag": "conv_789",
    "renotify": true,
    "requireInteraction": false,
    "silent": false,
    "vibrate": [200, 100, 200],
    "data": {
      "notification_id": "notif_abc123",
      "type": "message",
      "conversation_id": "conv_789",
      "message_id": "msg_456",
      "sender_id": "user_456",
      "action_url": "/messages/conv_789"
    },
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "reply",
        "title": "Reply",
        "icon": "https://skillsier.com/icons/reply.png"
      },
      {
        "action": "mark_read",
        "title": "Mark as Read",
        "icon": "https://skillsier.com/icons/check.png"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

6. Send push notification to each platform:  
   - **iOS:** HTTP/2 POST to APNS with JWT auth  
   - **Android:** HTTP POST to FCM with OAuth token  
   - **Web:** HTTP POST to push endpoint with VAPID signature  

7. For iOS (APNS):  
```bash
POST https://api.push.apple.com/3/device/{deviceToken}
Headers:
  authorization: bearer {jwt_token}
  apns-topic: com.skillsier.app
  apns-priority: 10
  apns-expiration: 0
Body: {JSON payload}
```

8. APNS returns response:  
```json
{
  "apns-id": "apns_123456",
  "status": 200
}
```

9. For Android (FCM):  
```bash
POST https://fcm.googleapis.com/v1/projects/skillsier/messages:send
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer {oauth_token}
  Content-Type: application/json
Body: {JSON payload}
```

10. FCM returns response:  
```json
{
  "name": "projects/skillsier/messages/0:1234567890",
  "success": true
}
```

11. For Web Push (VAPID):  
```bash
POST {subscription.endpoint}
Headers:
  TTL: 86400
  Content-Encoding: aes128gcm
  Authorization: vapid t={jwt},k={public_key}
Body: {Encrypted payload}
```

12. Web Push returns: `201 Created`  

13. Backend updates push_notification entity:  
```json
{
  "push_id": "push_abc123",
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "notification_id": "notif_abc123",
  "devices_sent": ["device_abc123", "device_xyz789", "device_web123"],
  "sent_at": "2025-01-15T14:30:00Z",
  "delivered_at": null,
  "clicked_at": null,
  "platforms": {
    "ios": { "status": "sent", "apns_id": "apns_123456" },
    "android": { "status": "sent", "fcm_message_id": "0:1234567890" },
    "web": { "status": "sent" }
  }
}
```

14. Publish `push.sent.v1` event

**A7: Receive Push Notification (Web)**  
1. Browser receives push message via service worker  
2. Service worker `push` event fires:  
```javascript
self.addEventListener('push', function(event) {
  const data = event.data.json();
  const options = {
    body: data.notification.body,
    icon: data.notification.icon,
    badge: data.notification.badge,
    tag: data.notification.tag,
    data: data.notification.data,
    actions: data.notification.actions,
    requireInteraction: data.notification.requireInteraction,
    vibrate: data.notification.vibrate
  };
  
  event.waitUntil(
    self.registration.showNotification(data.notification.title, options)
  );
});
```

**A8: Handle Notification Click (All Platforms)**  

**iOS:**  
1. User taps notification  
2. App launches (or comes to foreground)  
3. App delegate receives user response:  
```swift
func userNotificationCenter(_ center: UNUserNotificationCenter,
                           didReceive response: UNNotificationResponse) {
    let userInfo = response.notification.request.content.userInfo
    let conversationId = userInfo["conversation_id"] as? String
    
    // Navigate to conversation
    navigateToConversation(conversationId)
}
```
4. App navigates to target screen (conversation)  
5. Mark notification as read:  
   - Call: `PUT /v1/notifications/{notificationId}/read`  
6. Report click to backend:  
   - Call: `POST /v1/push/action` with action: "clicked"  
7. Publish `push.clicked.v1` event  

**Android:**  
1. User taps notification  
2. App launches via PendingIntent  
3. Intent contains notification data:  
```kotlin
val conversationId = intent.getStringExtra("conversation_id")
val notificationId = intent.getStringExtra("notification_id")
```
4. App navigates to target screen  
5. Mark as read and report click (same as iOS)  
6. Clear notification from shade:  
```kotlin
notificationManager.cancel(notificationId.hashCode())
```

**Web:**  
1. User clicks notification  
2. Service worker receives `notificationclick` event:  
```javascript
self.addEventListener('notificationclick', function(event) {
  event.notification.close();
  
  const data = event.notification.data;
  const actionUrl = data.action_url;
  
  event.waitUntil(
    clients.openWindow(actionUrl).then(function(windowClient) {
      // Report click
      fetch('/v1/push/action', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({
          notification_id: data.notification_id,
          action: 'clicked',
          timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
        })
      });
    })
  );
});
```
3. Browser opens/focuses tab with target URL  
4. Frontend marks notification as read  
5. Backend records click  

**A9: Handle Notification Action (Reply/Quick Actions)**  

**iOS:**  
1. User long-presses notification (3D Touch/Haptic Touch)  
2. iOS shows action buttons: "Reply", "Mark as Read"  
3. User taps "Reply"  
4. iOS shows text input field  
5. User types message: "Thanks! I'll review today."  
6. User taps "Send"  
7. App delegate receives text response:  
```swift
func userNotificationCenter(_ center: UNUserNotificationCenter,
                           didReceive response: UNNotificationResponse) {
    if let textResponse = response as? UNTextInputNotificationResponse {
        let messageText = textResponse.userText
        let conversationId = response.notification.request.content.userInfo["conversation_id"]
        
        // Send message via API
        sendMessage(conversationId: conversationId, text: messageText)
    }
}
```
8. Backend creates message in conversation  
9. Show success notification: "Message sent"  

**Android:**  
1. User swipes down on notification to reveal actions  
2. User taps "Reply"  
3. Android shows inline reply text field  
4. User types and sends  
5. BroadcastReceiver receives reply:  
```kotlin
val remoteInput = RemoteInput.getResultsFromIntent(intent)
val replyText = remoteInput?.getCharSequence("reply_key")
val conversationId = intent.getStringExtra("conversation_id")

// Send message via API
sendMessage(conversationId, replyText.toString())
```
6. Backend creates message  
7. Update notification: "Reply sent"  

**Web:**  
1. User clicks "Reply" action button  
2. Service worker receives `notificationclick` event with action:  
```javascript
self.addEventListener('notificationclick', function(event) {
  if (event.action === 'reply') {
    // Open conversation in window
    event.waitUntil(
      clients.openWindow('/messages/' + event.notification.data.conversation_id)
    );
  } else if (event.action === 'mark_read') {
    // Mark as read via API
    fetch('/v1/notifications/' + event.notification.data.notification_id + '/read', {
      method: 'PUT'
    });
    event.notification.close();
  }
});
```
3. Opens conversation window or performs action

**A11: Unregister Device / Disable Push**  
1. User navigates to device management  
2. User clicks "Remove" on a device  
3. Frontend confirms: "Remove this device from push notifications?"  
4. User confirms  
5. Call: `DELETE /v1/push/devices/{deviceId}`  
6. Backend:  
   - Mark device as inactive  
   - Set unregistered_at timestamp  
   - Remove device token from active pool  
7. Backend returns success  
8. Frontend removes device from list  
9. Show success message: "Device removed"  
10. Publish `device.unregistered.v1` event  

For web push unsubscribe:  
```javascript
const registration = await navigator.serviceWorker.ready;
const subscription = await registration.pushManager.getSubscription();
if (subscription) {
  await subscription.unsubscribe();
  // Then call backend to delete subscription
}
```

**A12: Send Test Push Notification**  
1. User clicks "Send Test Notification" button  
2. Call: `POST /v1/push/test` with user_id  
3. Backend validates:  
   - Check rate limit (5 per hour)  
   - Verify user has active devices  
4. Send test push to all devices:  
   - Title: "Test notification from Skillsier"  
   - Body: "If you see this, push notifications are working! ✅"  
5. User receives test notification on all devices  
6. Show success message: "Test notification sent!"
