#### Edge Cases & Conditional Branches

**Meeting Creation Issues:**

**EC1.** User tries to create meeting with conflicting time
- System queries connected calendars for conflicts
- Before creating, shows warning modal:
```
Scheduling Conflict Detected

You have existing events at this time:
• 2:00 PM - 3:00 PM: Weekly Team Meeting (Google Calendar)

Do you want to proceed anyway?
[Go Back]  [Create Anyway]
```
- If user proceeds, creates meeting but marks as potential conflict
- Sends notification about conflict to user

**EC2.** User tries to create meeting without adding participants
- System prevents creation with error: "Please add at least one participant"
- Highlight participants field
- For solo calendar blocking, suggest using "Block Time" feature instead

**EC3.** User tries to schedule meeting in the past
- System validates start_time > current time
- Shows error: "Cannot schedule meetings in the past"
- Auto-adjusts date/time to next available slot (current time + 1 hour, rounded)

**EC4.** Meeting title exceeds character limit (200 chars)
- Character counter shows 180/200, 200/200, 205/200 (red)
- Prevents submission if over limit
- Shows error: "Meeting title is too long (205/200 characters)"

**EC5.** Meeting duration exceeds 8 hours
- System shows warning: "Long meeting detected. Consider breaking into multiple sessions"
- Allows creation but suggests splitting
- Reminder scheduling adjusted for very long meetings

**RSVP & Invitation Issues:**

**EC6.** User tries to accept invitation after event has passed
- System detects event.start_time < NOW()
- Shows message: "This meeting has already occurred"
- RSVP actions disabled
- Shows "View Past Meeting" instead

**EC7.** User invited to meeting during their quiet hours
- Meeting shows with "During Quiet Hours" badge
- User can still accept but receives warning
- Option to request reschedule with suggested times

**EC8.** User responds "Tentative" to meeting
- RSVP status set to "tentative"
- Organizer notified: "Sarah marked as tentative"
- Meeting remains in user's calendar with "?" indicator
- User can later change to Accept/Decline

**EC9.** Required participant declines meeting
- Organizer receives urgent notification
- Meeting status changes to "At Risk"
- Organizer prompted: "Required participant declined. Reschedule or proceed without?"
- Options: Reschedule, Remove from Required, Proceed Anyway

**EC10.** Multiple participants, mixed RSVP statuses
- Meeting detail shows RSVP summary: "2 accepted, 1 declined, 1 pending"
- Visual indicators: ✓ green, ✗ red, ⏳ gray
- Organizer can send reminder to pending participants
- Auto-reminder sent 24 hours before meeting to pending RSVPs

**Calendar Integration Issues:**

**EC11.** Calendar sync fails (expired OAuth token)
- System attempts token refresh automatically
- If refresh fails, marks integration as "Connection Expired"
- User sees banner: "Google Calendar connection expired. Reconnect to continue syncing"
- [Reconnect] button triggers re-authorization flow
- Sync paused until reconnected

**EC12.** User connects calendar with 1000+ events
- Initial sync shows progress indicator: "Syncing... 234/1000 events"
- Sync performed in background (async job)
- User can continue using app while syncing
- Notification sent when complete: "Google Calendar sync complete. 1,247 events synced"
- If sync fails partway, resume from last successful event

**EC13.** Two-way sync creates duplicate events
- System uses event UID/external_id to detect duplicates
- Before creating duplicate, checks:
  - Same title
  - Same start/end time (within 5-minute tolerance)
  - Same participants
- If match found, links to existing event instead of creating new
- Sync log records "Duplicate prevented: matched existing event evt_123"

**EC14.** User disconnects calendar with synced events
- Shows confirmation: "Disconnect Google Calendar? X synced meetings will be kept in Skillsier"
- Options:
  - "Keep in Skillsier" - Events remain, sync stops
  - "Remove from Skillsier" - Deletes all synced events
- After disconnect, events marked with "Originally from Google Calendar" badge
- Cannot edit these events (read-only unless claimed)

**EC15.** Conflict between Skillsier meeting and external calendar event
- System detects overlap during sync
- Shows conflict notification with details of both events
- Options:
  - "Keep Both" - Both remain, user warned about double-booking
  - "Cancel Skillsier Meeting" - Cancel and notify participants
  - "Block External Time" - Mark external event as busy time only
- User preference saved for future conflicts

**Availability Sharing Issues:**

**EC16.** Availability link expires before someone books
- When recipient clicks expired link: "This availability link has expired"
- Shows message: "Please contact John Doe for new availability"
- Link creator notified: "Availability link avl-x7k9p2m expired. 0 bookings made"
- Option to extend expiration or generate new link

**EC17.** Multiple people try to book same time slot simultaneously
- First person to submit booking locks the slot
- Second person sees: "This time slot was just booked. Please select another time"
- Available slots list refreshes automatically
- No double-booking occurs (database transaction with row locking)

**EC18.** User's calendar changes after sharing availability link
- New conflict appears in previously available slot
- When someone tries to book conflicting slot:
  - System re-checks availability in real-time
  - If now unavailable: "This slot is no longer available"
  - Suggests nearest available alternatives
- Availability link automatically excludes newly busy times

**EC19.** Recipient books meeting outside working hours
- If user manipulates URL to book unavailable time:
  - Backend validates slot is in availability_slot table
  - Returns error: "Invalid time slot selected"
  - Prevents booking
- Frontend disables non-available time selection

**EC20.** User has no available slots in date range
- Modal shows: "No available slots found in this date range"
- Suggestions:
  - "Extend date range"
  - "Reduce meeting duration"
  - "Adjust working hours"
  - "Disable conflict checking"
- Cannot generate link with 0 available slots

**Meeting Reminders & Notifications:**

**EC21.** User has 10+ meetings in one day
- System sends consolidated reminder: "You have 12 meetings today"
- Lists next 3 upcoming meetings
- "View full schedule" link
- Individual reminders still sent 15 min before each
- Option to enable "Busy day mode" (fewer notifications)

**EC22.** Reminder notification fails to send
- System logs failed notification attempt
- Retries 3 times with exponential backoff (1 min, 5 min, 15 min)
- If all retries fail, logs error and moves on
- User may miss reminder (edge case, rare)
- Admin can monitor failed reminder rate

**EC23.** User changes meeting time after reminders scheduled
- System deletes old scheduled reminders
- Creates new reminders based on updated meeting time
- All participants notified of time change
- Email includes: "Meeting rescheduled: [Old time] → [New time]"
- Calendar integrations updated automatically

**EC24.** Meeting starts but participant hasn't joined
- 5 minutes after start time, organizer receives notification:
  - "Sarah Johnson hasn't joined the meeting yet"
- Option to send nudge notification
- "Waiting for participants" indicator in meeting interface

**Permissions & Access:**

**EC25.** Non-organizer tries to edit meeting
- Edit button hidden/disabled for non-organizers
- If API call attempted: Returns 403 Forbidden
- Error message: "Only the meeting organizer can edit this meeting"
- Exception: All participants can edit meeting notes/description (if enabled)

**EC26.** User tries to add external email (non-Skillsier user)
- System allows external email addresses
- External participant created as guest user
- Guest receives email invitation with limited access link
- Guest can view meeting details and RSVP via email only
- No Skillsier account required for guest participation

**EC27.** User tries to view another user's calendar
- Privacy setting: "Who can see my calendar?"
  - Everyone
  - My connections only
  - Clients/Freelancers I work with
  - No one
- If not authorized: "You don't have permission to view this calendar"
- Free/busy information may be visible even if details hidden

**Recurring Meetings:**

**EC28.** User creates weekly recurring meeting
- System generates series of calendar_event records
- Master event marked with recurrence_rule: "FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=12"
- Individual occurrences linked to master
- User can edit:
  - "This occurrence only"
  - "This and future occurrences"
  - "All occurrences"
- Deleting master deletes all future occurrences

**EC29.** User skips one occurrence of recurring meeting
- Select "Delete this occurrence only"
- System marks that specific occurrence as cancelled
- Doesn't affect other occurrences
- Participants notified: "Meeting on Jan 24 cancelled. Next meeting: Jan 31"

**EC30.** Participant declines single occurrence of recurring series
- RSVP applies to that occurrence only
- Other occurrences remain accepted
- Organizer notified: "Sarah declined Jan 24 meeting but is attending other occurrences"

**Time Zones & International:**

**EC31.** Meeting participants in different time zones
- Meeting stored in UTC in database
- Displayed to each user in their local timezone
- Meeting detail shows: "2:00 PM EST (11:00 AM PST)" for participants in different zones
- Invitation emails include timezone conversion
- Calendar integration syncs with correct timezone

**EC32.** User travels to different timezone
- System detects timezone change (browser/device)
- Shows notification: "Your timezone changed to Pacific Time. Update calendar?"
- Options:
  - "Update my timezone" - All meetings display in new timezone
  - "Keep original timezone" - Continue showing in home timezone
- Can manually change timezone in settings

**EC33.** Daylight Saving Time boundary
- Meeting scheduled during DST transition (e.g., "spring forward")
- System accounts for DST changes automatically
- If meeting at 2:00 AM on DST change day, warns user
- Reschedule suggestions shown for ambiguous times

**Mobile-Specific Edge Cases:**

**EC34.** User loses internet during meeting creation
- Form data saved in local storage
- When connection restored: "You have an unsaved meeting draft. Continue?"
- User can resume or discard
- Auto-save every 30 seconds while online

**EC35.** Calendar app closed during sync
- Background sync continues (iOS/Android background task)
- Notification shown when sync completes
- If background task killed, resumes on next app open
- Sync status persisted to handle interruptions

**EC36.** User receives meeting invitation while app closed
- Push notification received: "New meeting invitation from John Doe"
- Tap notification opens app directly to meeting details
- Quick actions in notification: "Accept" or "Decline"
- RSVP processed without opening app (background handler)

#### Accessibility Requirements

**Keyboard Navigation:**
- Calendar grid fully navigable with arrow keys
- Tab/Shift+Tab moves between calendar dates, meetings, and controls
- Enter/Space activates date selection and meeting details
- Escape closes modals and date pickers
- Keyboard shortcuts:
  - `T` - Jump to today
  - `N` - Create new meeting
  - `Left/Right arrows` - Navigate previous/next month
  - `Up/Down arrows` - Navigate weeks
  - `/` - Focus search

**Screen Reader Support:**
- Calendar dates announced with day, date, and event count
- "Monday, January 15, 2025, 3 events"
- Meeting time slots announced: "10:30 AM to 11:00 AM, Meeting with Sarah Johnson, Video Call"
- RSVP status announced: "Meeting invitation from John Doe, status pending"
- Integration status announced: "Google Calendar connected, last synced 2 minutes ago"
- Availability slots announced: "10:30 AM to 11:00 AM, available"
- Loading states announced: "Loading calendar events"
- Success/error messages announced immediately with role="alert"

**Visual Accessibility:**
- Minimum contrast ratio 4.5:1 for all text and controls
- Meeting status indicators use both color and icons:
  - Accepted: Green checkmark + "Accepted" text
  - Declined: Red X + "Declined" text
  - Pending: Gray clock + "Pending" text
  - Tentative: Yellow question mark + "Tentative" text
- Focus indicators visible with 2px outline
- Color-blind friendly palette (avoid red/green only distinctions)
- Meeting conflicts indicated with icon + text, not color alone
- Time zone differences shown with text, not just color coding

**Mobile Accessibility:**
- Touch targets minimum 44x44pt (iOS) / 48x48dp (Android)
- Swipe gestures for navigation (swipe between days/weeks)
- VoiceOver/TalkBack full support for all interactive elements
- Haptic feedback on important actions (meeting created, RSVP sent)
- Dynamic Type support for text scaling
- Reduce Motion respected (fade transitions instead of slides)
- Calendar dates easily tappable (large touch targets)

**Form Accessibility:**
- All form fields have visible labels
- Required fields clearly marked with asterisk and text
- Date/time pickers accessible via keyboard and screen reader
- Validation errors associated with fields via aria-describedby
- Error summary at top of form for multiple errors
- Autocomplete attributes for name, email fields

---

#### Performance Targets

**Web Application:**
- Calendar page initial load: <1.2 seconds
- Month view rendering (30 days + events): <500ms
- Day view rendering (timeline + events): <400ms
- Meeting creation modal open: <200ms
- Meeting details page load: <800ms
- Calendar integration settings load: <600ms
- Availability link generation: <2 seconds
- Calendar sync trigger response: <300ms (async processing)
- RSVP action response: <500ms
- Search meetings results: <600ms

**Mobile Application:**
- Calendar home screen render: <800ms
- Month view with events: <500ms
- Day view timeline render: <400ms
- Create meeting screen open: <300ms
- Meeting details screen load: <600ms
- Calendar integration screen load: <500ms
- Availability generation: <2 seconds
- Pull-to-refresh sync: <1.5 seconds
- RSVP action response: <400ms
- Smooth scrolling at 60fps

**Backend Performance:**
- Create calendar event: <300ms
- Retrieve events (monthly): <200ms
- RSVP update: <150ms
- Calendar sync (per 100 events): <2 seconds
- Availability calculation: <1.5 seconds
- Conflict detection: <500ms
- Recurring event generation: <1 second (per 20 occurrences)
- Meeting invitation send: <400ms
- External calendar API calls: <2 seconds (with timeout)

**Database Queries:**
- Event lookup by ID: <30ms (indexed)
- Events by date range: <100ms (indexed on start_time, user_id)
- Participant RSVP status: <40ms (indexed on event_id, user_id)
- Integration status check: <50ms (indexed on user_id, provider)
- Availability slots query: <80ms (indexed on availability_link_id)
- Conflict detection query: <150ms (indexed on user_id, time range)

**Caching Strategy:**
- Calendar events cached for 5 minutes
- Integration status cached for 2 minutes
- Availability link data cached for 10 minutes
- User calendar preferences cached for 15 minutes
- External calendar sync results cached for sync frequency interval
- Cache invalidation on updates

---

#### Security Measures

**OAuth & Integration Security:**
- OAuth 2.0 for all calendar integrations
- Access tokens encrypted at rest (AES-256)
- Refresh tokens stored in secrets manager
- Token rotation every 90 days
- Revoked tokens immediately invalidated
- OAuth state parameter validated to prevent CSRF
- Redirect URI whitelist enforced
- Integration connection requires re-authentication if suspicious activity detected

**Meeting Access Control:**
- Only participants can view meeting details
- Only organizer can edit/delete meetings
- Guest access via time-limited tokens (24-hour expiry)
- Meeting links contain random secure tokens
- Video call links generated with cryptographically secure random values
- Unauthorized access attempts logged and monitored

**Availability Link Security:**
- Link codes generated with secure random (128-bit entropy)
- Links expire after configured duration (max 30 days)
- Rate limiting on booking attempts (5 per 15 minutes per IP)
- No PII exposed in availability link data
- Booking requires email verification (confirmation email sent)
- Suspicious booking patterns trigger admin alert

**Data Protection:**
- Meeting details encrypted at rest
- Video call links encrypted
- External calendar tokens encrypted
- Participant email addresses hashed for analytics
- GDPR-compliant data retention (meetings older than 2 years archived)
- User can delete meeting history
- Calendar sync logs retain no PII

**Rate Limiting:**
- Meeting creation: 20 per hour per user
- RSVP updates: 50 per hour per user
- Calendar sync: 6 per hour per integration (max)
- Availability link generation: 10 per day per user
- API endpoints protected with sliding window rate limiting
- Burst allowance for legitimate use cases

**Audit Logging:**
- All meeting CRUD operations logged
- Calendar integration connections/disconnections logged
- RSVP changes logged with timestamp and IP
- Availability link accesses logged
- Failed authentication attempts logged
- Admin actions on meetings logged
- Logs retained for 1 year

- `wo-comments-combined-fe-folder-structure.md` (calendar components, hooks, API clients)
- `apps/web/app/(authenticated)/calendar/` (web calendar interface)
- `apps/mobile/app/(authenticated)/calendar/` (mobile calendar screens)
- `packages/ui/src/components/calendar/` (shared calendar components)
- `packages/ui/src/components/meeting/` (meeting components)
- `packages/hooks/src/useCalendar.ts` (calendar state management)
- `packages/api-client/src/lib/calendar.ts` (calendar API client)

**Third-Party Integrations:**
- Google Calendar API v3
- Microsoft Graph API (Outlook Calendar)
- Apple CalDAV
- iCalendar (.ics) format specification (RFC 5545)
- OAuth 2.0 specification (RFC 6749)
- Zoom/Google Meet video conference APIs (for meeting link generation)

**Standards & Protocols:**
- iCalendar (RFC 5545) - Calendar data exchange
- iTIP (RFC 5546) - iCalendar Transport-Independent Interoperability Protocol
- CalDAV (RFC 4791) - Calendar access protocol
- OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749) - Authorization framework
- Recurrence Rule (RRULE) specification
- Time Zone Database (IANA tz database)
- ISO 8601 (Date and time format)

**Calendar Integration Documentation:**
- Google Calendar API documentation
- Microsoft Graph Calendar API documentation
- Apple Calendar Server documentation
- CalDAV specification and best practices

## COM-18 — Video/Audio Calls (Web & Mobile)

### ID
COM-18

### Persona
All Users (Freelancers, Clients, Admins - any authenticated user engaged in conversations)

### Description
Comprehensive voice and video calling system enabling users to initiate, receive, and manage real-time audio/video calls with features including WebRTC-based connectivity, call recording, screen sharing, call history, quality monitoring, missed call tracking, and integration with conversations and calendar events. Supports 1-on-1 and group calls (up to 10 participants) with advanced features like call quality indicators, automatic reconnection, and device management.

### Preconditions & Triggers

### Triggers
* User clicks "Video Call" or "Audio Call" button in conversation header
* User receives incoming call notification and clicks to answer
* User initiates call from user profile quick actions
* User clicks on missed call notification to call back
* User starts scheduled call from calendar event
* User joins ongoing call from conversation
* User initiates emergency call to support (admin feature)
* System auto-initiates call for scheduled interviews
* User clicks call link from email/SMS notification
* User tests call quality in settings

### Preconditions
* User is authenticated
* User has active account (not suspended)
* Target user(s) exist and are available for calls
* User has granted camera/microphone permissions (for video/audio)
* Browser/app supports WebRTC (Chrome 70+, Safari 14+, Firefox 80+)
* Network connectivity is stable (minimum 1 Mbps for audio, 2 Mbps for video)
* User is not already in an active call (unless adding participants)
* For scheduled calls: User has valid calendar event with call details
* For call recording: User has recording permissions enabled
* Call limits not exceeded (max concurrent calls per tenant)

## Primary Screens

### Web
* (dashboard)/messages/[conversationId]/call/page.tsx — In-call interface (video/audio)
* (dashboard)/messages/[conversationId]/call/incoming/page.tsx — Incoming call screen

* (dashboard)/calls/recordings/page.tsx — Call recordings library

  * call/entity.go — Core call entity
  * call_participant/entity.go — Call participant management
  * call_recording/entity.go — Call recording metadata
  * call_quality/entity.go — Call quality metrics
  * POST /v1/calls — Initiate call
  * POST /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/calls — Create call in conversation context
  * GET /v1/calls/{id} — Get call details

  * DELETE /v1/calls/{id}/participants/{user_id} — Remove participant from call

  * POST /v1/calls/{id}/sdp-offer — Send SDP offer (WebRTC)
  * POST /v1/calls/{id}/sdp-answer — Send SDP answer (WebRTC)

  * POST /v1/calls/{id}/feedback — Submit call quality feedback
  * GET /v1/calls/{id}/recording — Get recording metadata
  * GET /v1/calls/{id}/participants — List call participants
* users-be:
  * GET /v1/users/{id} — Get user details for call participants

* storage-be:
  * POST /v1/storage/recordings — Upload call recording
  * GET /v1/storage/recordings/{id} — Download call recording
  * DELETE /v1/storage/recordings/{id} — Delete call recording
  * POST /v1/storage/screen-recordings — Upload screen recording

* notifications-be:
  * POST /v1/notifications/call-incoming — Send incoming call notification

* calendar-be:
  * GET /v1/calendar/events/{id} — Get calendar event details (for scheduled calls)
  * PUT /v1/calendar/events/{id}/call-link — Update event with call link

* contracts-be:
  * GET /v1/contracts/{id} — Get contract details (for contract-related calls)

* jobs-be:
  * GET /v1/jobs/{id}/interviews — Get interview calls

* admin-be:

* WebRTC Signaling Server:
  * WebSocket connection: wss://api.skillsier.com/v1/signaling
  * ICE candidate exchange (real-time)

  * Bandwidth negotiation
* Events:
  * Publish: call.initiated.v1, call.accepted.v1, call.rejected.v1, call.ice_candidate.exchanged.v1, call.ended.v1, call.missed.v1, call.quality_recorded.v1, call.participant.joined.v1, call.participant.left.v1, call.recording.started.v1, call.recording.stopped.v1, call.recording.ready.v1, call.screen_share.started.v1, call.screen_share.stopped.v1, call.reconnecting.v1, call.reconnected.v1, call.quality.degraded.v1

## Flow Steps (Happy Path)

### A1: Initiate Outgoing Call
1. User navigates to conversation or user profile
2. User clicks "Call" button in header/profile
3. System displays call type selector (if not pre-selected):
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Start Call                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌───────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐│
│  │  🎤 Audio     │  │  📹 Video    ││
│  │               │  │              ││
│  │  Voice call   │  │  Video call  ││
│  │  only         │  │  with camera ││
│  └───────────────┘  └──────────────┘│
│                                     │
│  [Cancel]                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```
4. User selects call type (Audio or Video)
5. System performs pre-call checks:
* Check permissions:
```typescript
// Web
const stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({
  audio: true,
  video: callType === 'VIDEO'
});

// Mobile
const { status } = await Camera.requestPermissionsAsync();
const { status: audioStatus } = await Audio.requestPermissionsAsync();
```
* If permissions denied: Show permission request dialog with instructions
* Check network connectivity: Minimum 1 Mbps for audio, 2 Mbps for video
* Check participant availability via presence API
6. API Call: POST /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/calls
```json
{
  "call_type": "VIDEO",
  "participants": [
    {
      "user_id": "uuid-recipient",
      "role": "PARTICIPANT"
    }
  ],
  "conversation_id": "uuid-conversation",
  "timeout_sec": 30,
  "metadata": {
    "initiated_from": "conversation_header",
    "device_type": "web"
  }
}
```
7. System creates call session with status: INITIATED
8. Response includes:
```json
{
  "call_id": "uuid-call",
  "status": "INITIATED",
  "call_type": "VIDEO",
  "caller_id": "uuid-caller",
  "participants": [...],
  "ice_servers": [...],
  "expires_at": "2025-01-15T10:05:30Z",
  "signaling_url": "wss://api.skillsier.com/v1/signaling?call_id=uuid-call&token=...",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:05:00Z"
}
```
9. System navigates to outgoing call screen: (dashboard)/messages/[conversationId]/call
10. Display calling interface:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ← Back                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                     │
│         👤 Sarah Johnson            │
│                                     │
│         Calling...                  │
│                                     │
│         ⭕ Ringing                  │
│      (animated pulsing ring)        │
│                                     │
│                                     │
│  [🔇 Mute]  [📹 Camera Off]         │
│                                     │
│        [📞 End Call]                │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```
11. System publishes event: call.initiated.v1
12. System schedules automatic timeout job: MarkMissedCallJob (runs at expires_at)
13. Frontend establishes WebSocket connection to signaling server
14. Wait for recipient to accept/reject (max 30 seconds)

### A2: Receive Incoming Call
1. Recipient receives event via WebSocket: call.initiated.v1
2. System displays incoming call notification:
Web (Banner):
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 📞 Incoming Video Call                          │
│ 👤 John Doe is calling you...                  │
│ [✅ Accept]  [❌ Decline]  [👋 Ignore]         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
Mobile (Full Screen):
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                     │
│                                     │
│         👤 John Doe                 │
│                                     │
│       📹 Video Call                 │
│                                     │
│      ⭕⭕⭕ Ringing               │
│    (animated + ringtone)            │
│                                     │
│                                     │
│  ┌─────────┐         ┌────────────┐│
│  │    ❌   │         │     ✅     ││
│  │ Decline │         │   Accept   ││
│  └─────────┘         └────────────┘│
│                                     │
│         [👋 Ignore]                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```
3. System plays ringtone (mobile) or notification sound (web)
4. Browser/mobile notification sent (if app in background):
* Title: "Incoming Call from John Doe"
* Body: "Video call"
* Actions: ["Accept", "Decline"]
5. Quick actions available:
* Accept: Proceed to in-call interface
* Decline: Reject call with reason (optional)
* Ignore: Let it ring until timeout
6. If no action within 30 seconds: System auto-marks as missed

### A3: Accept Call & Establish Connection
1. Recipient clicks "Accept" button
2. System requests permissions (if not already granted):
```typescript
const stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({
  audio: true,
  video: callType === 'VIDEO'
});
```
3. API Call: PUT /v1/calls/{call_id}/accept
```json
{
  "user_id": "uuid-recipient",
  "device_info": {
    "device_type": "mobile",
    "os": "iOS",
    "browser": "Safari"
  }
}
```
4. System updates call status: INITIATED → ACCEPTED
5. Response includes WebRTC configuration:
```json
{
  "status": "ACCEPTED",
  "ice_servers": [
    {
      "urls": ["stun:stun.skillsier.com:3478"]
    },
    {
      "urls": ["turn:turn.skillsier.com:3478"],
      "username": "temp-user",
      "credential": "temp-pass"
    }
  ],
  "signaling_url": "wss://...",
  "accepted_at": "2025-01-15T10:05:15Z"
}
```
6. Cancel scheduled timeout job: CancelMissedTimer(call_id)
7. System publishes event: call.accepted.v1
8. WebRTC Connection Establishment:
a. Caller creates RTCPeerConnection:
```typescript
const peerConnection = new RTCPeerConnection({
  iceServers: [...],
  iceCandidatePoolSize: 10
});

// Add local tracks
localStream.getTracks().forEach(track => {
  peerConnection.addTrack(track, localStream);
});
```
b. Caller creates SDP offer:
```typescript
const offer = await peerConnection.createOffer({
  offerToReceiveAudio: true,
  offerToReceiveVideo: callType === 'VIDEO'
});
await peerConnection.setLocalDescription(offer);
```
c. Send SDP offer via signaling:
```typescript
// POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/sdp-offer
{
  "sdp": offer.sdp,
  "type": "offer",
  "from_user_id": "uuid-caller"
}
```
d. Recipient receives SDP offer via WebSocket
e. Recipient creates answer:
```typescript
await peerConnection.setRemoteDescription(offer);
const answer = await peerConnection.createAnswer();
await peerConnection.setLocalDescription(answer);
```
f. Send SDP answer via signaling:
```typescript
// POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/sdp-answer
{
  "sdp": answer.sdp,
  "type": "answer",
  "from_user_id": "uuid-recipient"
}
```
g. Caller sets remote description
h. ICE Candidate Exchange:
```typescript
peerConnection.onicecandidate = (event) => {
  if (event.candidate) {
    // POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/ice-candidates
    {
      "candidate": event.candidate.candidate,
      "sdpMLineIndex": event.candidate.sdpMLineIndex,
      "from_user_id": currentUserId
    }
  }
};

// Receive ICE candidates via WebSocket
socket.on('ice-candidate', async (candidate) => {
  await peerConnection.addIceCandidate(candidate);
});
```
i. Wait for connection state: connected
```typescript
peerConnection.onconnectionstatechange = () => {
  if (peerConnection.connectionState === 'connected') {
    updateCallStatus('CONNECTED');
    startCallTimer();
  }
};
```
9. Navigate both users to in-call interface
10. Update call status: ACCEPTED → CONNECTED
11. Start call duration timer
12. System publishes event: call.connected.v1

### A4: In-Call Interface (Video Call)
1. Display video call interface:
Web Layout:
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ← Back    Sarah Johnson    ⚙️ Settings        │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
```

2. Video Rendering:
```typescript
// Remote video
peerConnection.ontrack = (event) => {
  const [remoteStream] = event.streams;
  remoteVideoElement.srcObject = remoteStream;
};

// Local video (self-view)
localVideoElement.srcObject = localStream;
```
3. Call Info Display:
* Participant name(s)
* Call duration timer (format: MM:SS or HH:MM:SS)
* Connection quality indicator:
  * 🟢 Green: Excellent (RTT < 100ms, packet loss < 1%)
  * 🟡 Yellow: Good (RTT 100-300ms, packet loss 1-3%)
  * 🔴 Red: Poor (RTT > 300ms, packet loss > 3%)
* Network type indicator (Wi-Fi, 4G, 5G)
4. Call Controls:
A. Mute/Unmute Audio:
```typescript
const toggleMute = async () => {
  const audioTrack = localStream.getAudioTracks()[0];
  audioTrack.enabled = !audioTrack.enabled;
  setIsMuted(!audioTrack.enabled);
  
  // Send mute status to other participants
  socket.emit('audio-muted', { 
    callId, 
    userId, 
    isMuted: !audioTrack.enabled 
  });
};
```
* Button icon changes: 🎤 (unmuted) ↔ 🔇 (muted)
* Visual indicator on remote participant when they mute
* Keyboard shortcut: Space (push to talk) or M (toggle)
B. Toggle Video:
```typescript
const toggleVideo = async () => {
  const videoTrack = localStream.getVideoTracks()[0];
  videoTrack.enabled = !videoTrack.enabled;
  setIsVideoOn(videoTrack.enabled);
  
  socket.emit('video-toggled', { 
    callId, 
    userId, 
    isVideoOn: videoTrack.enabled 
  });
};
```
* Button icon changes: 📹 (on) ↔ 📹❌ (off)
* When off: Show avatar/initials in local video
* Keyboard shortcut: V
C. Screen Share:
```typescript
const startScreenShare = async () => {
  try {
    const screenStream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia({
      video: {
        cursor: 'always',
        displaySurface: 'monitor' // or 'window', 'browser'
      },
      audio: false
    });
    
    // Replace video track with screen track
    const screenTrack = screenStream.getVideoTracks()[0];
    const sender = peerConnection.getSenders()
      .find(s => s.track.kind === 'video');
    await sender.replaceTrack(screenTrack);
    
    setIsScreenSharing(true);
    
    // Handle screen share stopped
    screenTrack.onended = () => {
      stopScreenShare();
    };
    
    // POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/screen-share/start
    socket.emit('screen-share-started', { callId, userId });
    
  } catch (error) {
    showError('Screen sharing not supported or permission denied');
  }
};
```
* Shows screen picker dialog (choose screen/window/tab)
* Remote participant sees screen instead of video
* Banner: "You're sharing your screen" (with Stop button)
* Only one participant can share at a time
* Auto-stops if user switches windows/tabs (browser security)
* Mobile: Limited support (Android only, requires Android 11+)
D. In-Call Chat:
* Opens chat sidebar (web) or bottom sheet (mobile)
* Text chat continues without leaving call
* Messages saved to conversation thread
* Notification dot when new message received
E. Settings:

* Video Device:

* Speaker/Output:

5. Connection Quality Monitoring:
```typescript
setInterval(async () => {
  const stats = await peerConnection.getStats();
  stats.forEach(report => {
    if (report.type === 'inbound-rtp') {
      const packetsLost = report.packetsLost;
      const packetsReceived = report.packetsReceived;
      const packetLossRate = packetsLost / (packetsLost + packetsReceived);
      
      // Calculate RTT
      const rtt = report.roundTripTime * 1000; // ms
      
      // Update quality indicator
      if (rtt < 100 && packetLossRate < 0.01) {
        setQuality('excellent'); // 🟢
      } else if (rtt < 300 && packetLossRate < 0.03) {
        setQuality('good'); // 🟡
      } else {
        setQuality('poor'); // 🔴
      }
      
      // Submit metrics to backend
      if (Date.now() - lastMetricSubmit > 10000) {
        submitQualityMetrics({
          call_id: callId,
          rtt,
          packet_loss_rate: packetLossRate,
          jitter: report.jitter,
          bandwidth: report.bytesReceived / timeDelta
        });
      }
    }
  });
}, 2000);
```
6. Quality Degradation Handling:
* If quality drops to "poor": Show banner "Poor connection detected. Reducing video quality..."
* Auto-adjust bitrate:
```typescript
if (quality === 'poor') {
  const sender = peerConnection.getSenders()
    .find(s => s.track.kind === 'video');
  const params = sender.getParameters();
  params.encodings[0].maxBitrate = 500000; // 500 kbps
  await sender.setParameters(params);
}
```
* Suggest switching to audio-only

```typescript
const upgradeToVideo = async () => {

};
```

### A8: Record Call
1. User clicks "Record" button (⏺️)

4. If any participant declines: Recording not started
5. If all consent: API Call: POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/recording/start
6. System starts recording:
```typescript
const mediaRecorder = new MediaRecorder(combinedStream, {
  mimeType: 'video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus',
  videoBitsPerSecond: 2500000
});

const chunks = [];
mediaRecorder.ondataavailable = (e) => chunks.push(e.data);
mediaRecorder.onstop = async () => {
  const blob = new Blob(chunks, { type: 'video/webm' });
  await uploadRecording(callId, blob);
};

mediaRecorder.start(1000); // 1s chunks
```

```
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

9. To stop: Click "Stop Recording"
10. API Call: POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/recording/stop
11. System processes and uploads recording:
* Combine audio/video tracks
* Generate thumbnail from first frame
* Upload to storage-be
* Create call_recording entry
12. When ready: Notify participants "Call recording ready"

## Edge Cases & Branches

### Call Initiation & Setup
EC1. User initiates call but recipient is offline
* System checks recipient presence
* Show message: "Sarah Johnson is currently offline. Send message instead?"
* Options:
  * "Send Message"
  * "Try Anyway" (sends notification, may go to voicemail feature in future)
  * "Cancel"
EC2. User initiates call but microphone permission denied
* Browser/OS shows permission prompt
* If denied: Show error modal:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Microphone Access Required         │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Skillsier needs microphone access  │
│  to make calls.                     │
│                                     │
│  How to enable:                     │
│  1. Click the 🔒 icon in address bar│
│  2. Allow microphone access         │
│  3. Refresh the page                │
│                                     │
│  [Open Settings]  [Cancel]          │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```
* Provide OS-specific instructions (Chrome, Safari, Firefox)
* "Open Settings" button deep-links to browser permissions
EC3. User initiates video call but camera not available
* Check if camera exists: navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices()
* If no camera: Auto-downgrade to audio call
* Show notification: "Camera not detected. Starting audio call instead."
* User can enable video later if camera becomes available
EC4. Recipient busy (already on another call)
* Check active call status via presence API
* Show caller: "Sarah Johnson is currently on another call"
* Options:
  * "Leave Voicemail" (if voicemail feature enabled)
  * "Send Message"
  * "Cancel"
* Send push notification to recipient: "Missed call from John Doe (you were on another call)"
EC5. No answer (timeout after 30 seconds)
* Call status remains INITIATED for 30 seconds
* If not accepted: MarkMissedCallJob executes automatically
* Update status: INITIATED → MISSED
* Caller sees: "No answer. Call ended."
* Recipient gets missed call notification
* Call saved to history as "Missed Call"
* Event published: call.missed.v1
EC6. Recipient rejects call
* API Call: PUT /v1/calls/{call_id}/reject
* Optional reject reason:
  * "Busy"
  * "In a meeting"
  * "Can't talk now"
  * Custom message
* Caller sees: "Call declined by Sarah Johnson"
* Reason displayed if provided: "Sarah Johnson declined (Busy)"
* Call saved to history as "Rejected"
* No missed call notification sent
EC7. Multiple devices (recipient has web + mobile online)
* System sends call notification to all devices
* Ring all devices simultaneously
* First device to accept wins
* Other devices automatically dismissed
* If timeout: All devices show missed call
EC8. User has Do Not Disturb enabled
* Check DND status before ringing
* If DND active:
  * No sound/vibration
  * Show silent notification: "Incoming call (Silent)"
  * Call goes to missed after timeout
  * Exception: "Priority contacts" can break through DND

### Connection & Quality
EC9. Poor network during call (high packet loss)
* Monitor quality metrics every 2 seconds
* If packet loss > 5% for 10 seconds:
  * Show banner: "⚠️ Poor connection detected"
  * Auto-reduce video quality: 720p → 480p → 360p
  * If still poor: Suggest audio-only
  * Show "Switch to Audio Only" button
* User can manually adjust quality in settings
EC10. Network drops completely during call
* WebRTC connection state changes to disconnected
* Show "Reconnecting..." overlay with spinner
* System attempts to reconnect:
  * Re-establish WebRTC connection
  * Exchange new ICE candidates
  * Restore audio/video streams
* If reconnected within 10 seconds:
  * Resume call seamlessly
  * Show success message: "Reconnected"
  * Event: call.reconnected.v1
* If not reconnected after 30 seconds:
  * End call automatically
  * Show "Call ended due to connection issues"
  * Save as completed call with reconnection note
EC11. Only TURN server reachable (blocked P2P)
* ICE gathering fails for STUN (corporate firewall)
* System falls back to TURN relay
* Connection established but with higher latency
* Show info: "Using relay connection (may have higher latency)"
* Call quality indicator may show yellow
EC12. Browser doesn't support required codecs
* Check codec support: RTCRtpSender.getCapabilities('video')
* If VP9 not supported: Fall back to H.264
* If no video codec: Show error:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Video Call Not Supported           │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Your browser doesn't support video │
│  calls. Please use:                 │
│  • Chrome 70+                       │
│  • Safari 14+                       │
│  • Firefox 80+                      │
│  • Edge 79+                         │
│                                     │
│  [Switch to Audio Call]  [Cancel]   │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```
EC13. High CPU usage (device overheating)
* Monitor CPU usage via navigator.getBattery() (if available)
* If device heating or CPU > 80%:
  * Show warning: "Device is working hard. Reduce video quality?"
  * Auto-reduce resolution if user agrees
  * Disable background blur (computationally expensive)
  * Suggest audio-only mode
EC14. Bandwidth insufficient for selected quality
* Monitor bandwidth: RTCStatsReport.availableOutgoingBitrate
* If available bandwidth < required:
  * Auto-reduce quality to match bandwidth
  * Show notification: "Video quality adjusted to match connection"
  * Quality ladder:
    * 720p (HD) → 480p (SD) → 360p (LD) → 240p (Very Low)
    * 2.5 Mbps → 1 Mbps → 500 kbps → 250 kbps
EC15. Symmetric NAT (NAT traversal fails)
* Both peers behind symmetric NAT
* Direct P2P connection fails
* System must use TURN relay
* Check TURN connectivity before showing error
* If TURN also fails: Show error:
```
Unable to establish connection. Please check your network settings
or contact support.
[Retry]  [Report Issue]
```

### Screen Sharing
EC16. Screen share on unsupported browser
* Check: navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia
* If not available (older browsers):
  * Disable screen share button
  * Tooltip: "Screen sharing not supported in this browser"
  * Suggest upgrading browser
EC17. User denies screen share permission
* getDisplayMedia() throws NotAllowedError
* Show message: "Screen sharing permission denied"
* Button remains clickable for retry
* No persistent error state
EC18. User stops screen share from browser UI
* Browser's "Stop sharing" button clicked
* screenTrack.onended event fires
* System automatically stops screen share:
  * Replace screen track with camera track
  * Replace screen track with camera track
  * Show success message: "Screen sharing stopped"
* API Call: POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/screen-share/stop
EC19. Multiple users try to share screen simultaneously
* First user starts sharing → Success
* Second user tries to start → Show error:
```
Only one participant can share screen at a time.
Sarah Johnson is currently sharing. Wait for them to stop.
[Notify Me When Available]  [OK]
```
* "Notify Me" button sends notification when screen share stops
EC20. Screen share with audio (system audio)
* Check if browser supports audio sharing (Chrome only)
* If available: Add checkbox "Share audio" in screen picker
* If selected: Include system audio in stream
* Show indicator: "🔊 Sharing screen with audio"
* Not available on Safari/Firefox: Show info tooltip

### Call Recording
EC21. Participant declines recording consent
* One participant clicks "No" on consent dialog
* Recording cannot start (legal requirement)
* Show message to initiator: "Recording cannot start. [Name] declined."
* Options:
  * "Continue Without Recording"
  * "Ask Again" (limited to 1 retry)
  * "End Call"
* If critical: User may choose to end call
EC22. Recording storage quota exceeded
* Check storage before starting: GET /v1/storage/quota
* If quota full:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Storage Full                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  You've used 10 GB / 10 GB of       │
│  recording storage.                 │
│                                     │
│  Delete old recordings or upgrade   │
│  your plan to continue recording.   │
│                                     │
│  [Manage Recordings]  [Upgrade]     │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```
* Disable recording button until space freed
EC23. Recording upload fails (network error)
* Call ends, recording saved locally
* Upload to storage-be fails (network issue)
* System queues for retry:
  * Retry every 5 minutes (max 10 attempts)
  * Show notification: "Recording upload pending..."
  * If all retries fail: Show error with manual upload option
* User can manually trigger upload from recordings list
EC24. Browser tab closed during recording
* Recording stops automatically (MediaRecorder requires active context)
* Partial recording saved if ondataavailable fired
* When user reopens: Show notification:
```
Recording was interrupted when the tab closed.
Partial recording saved (8m 34s of 15m 23s).
[View Recording]  [Discard]
```
EC25. Recording too long (exceeds limit)
* Max recording length: 2 hours (configurable per plan)
* At 1h 50m: Show warning "Recording will stop in 10 minutes"
* At 2h: Auto-stop recording
* Save as complete recording
* Show notification: "Recording stopped (max duration reached)"

### Group Calls
EC26. Max participants reached (10 users)
* User tries to add 11th participant
* Show error:
```
Maximum participants reached (10/10).
Remove a participant to add someone new.
[OK]
```
* Disable "Add Participant" button
EC27. Participant joins mid-call
* New participant added via "Add Participant"
* They receive call invitation
* Upon accepting: Establish connections with all existing participants
* Show join notification to all: "Michael Chen joined the call"
* Update participant list
* Adjust video layout for new count
EC28. Participant leaves mid-call (not host)
* Participant clicks "Leave Call" (not "End Call")
* Their connections close
* Show notification to others: "Sarah Johnson left the call"
* Remove from participant list
* Adjust video layout
* Call continues for remaining participants
EC29. Host leaves group call
* If host clicks "End Call": Show options:
  * "End Call for Everyone"
  * "Leave Call (continue for others)"
* If "End for Everyone": All participants disconnected, call ends
* If "Leave": Host leaves, call continues, new host assigned (first joined)
EC30. Participant connection drops in group call
* One participant's connection fails
* Show to others: "Michael Chen is reconnecting..."
* If reconnected within 30s: Resume seamlessly
* If timeout: Remove from call
* Show: "Michael Chen disconnected"
* Call continues for others
EC31. Poor connection for one participant in group
* Monitor individual quality metrics
* If one user has poor quality:
  * Suggest they switch to audio-only
  * Don't degrade quality for others
  * Show indicator next to their name: "🔴 Poor connection"

### Mobile-Specific
EC32. Incoming call while app in background
* Push notification with call actions
* Full-screen call UI displays (CallKit on iOS)
* Ringtone plays even if phone is on silent
* Answer from lock screen available
* Swipe actions: Accept / Decline
EC33. User switches apps during call
* Call continues in background (Picture-in-Picture on Android 8+, iOS 14+)
* Show floating PiP window:
  * Small video preview (draggable)
  * Mute button
  * End call button
* Tap PiP to return to full call screen
EC34. Incoming call while on first
* System call takes precedence
* Skillsier call auto-paused
* Show notification: "Call paused (incoming phone call)"
* When system call ends: Show "Resume Call?" dialog
* User can resume or end Skillsier call
EC35. Low battery during call
* Monitor battery level
* At 20%: Show warning "Low battery. Consider plugging in."
* At 10%: Suggest switching to audio-only to save battery
* At 5%: Auto-switch to audio-only
EC36. Bluetooth headset disconnects during call
* Audio device changes from Bluetooth to speaker
* Show notification: "Bluetooth disconnected. Using speaker."
* When Bluetooth reconnects: Show "Switch to Bluetooth?"
EC37. Camera switch during video call (front/back)
* User clicks "Switch Camera" button
* System enumerates available cameras
* Seamlessly switch video track:
```typescript
const newStream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({
  video: { facingMode: isFrontCamera ? 'environment' : 'user' }
});
const newVideoTrack = newStream.getVideoTracks()[0];
const sender = peerConnection.getSenders()
  .find(s => s.track.kind === 'video');
await sender.replaceTrack(newVideoTrack);
```
* No interruption to call
EC38. App crashes/force-closes during call
* Call disconnected from user's end
* Other participants see: "John Doe disconnected"
* Call saved as "Interrupted" in history
* When app reopens: Show "Resume Call?" if call still active

EC43. Echo detected during call

EC44. Duplicate tab with same call

```
Opening here will end the call in the other tab.
```

```
[View Calendar]  [Message Organizer]
```

### Advanced Features
EC48. Background blur during video call
* User enables "Background Blur" in settings
* System checks if SegmentationModel available
* If supported:
```typescript
const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
const model = await bodyPix.load();

const applyBlur = async () => {
  const segmentation = await model.segmentPerson(videoElement);
  const backgroundBlurAmount = 15;
  const edgeBlurAmount = 3;
  const flipHorizontal = false;
  
  bodyPix.drawBokehEffect(
    canvas, videoElement, segmentation,
    backgroundBlurAmount, edgeBlurAmount, flipHorizontal
  );
  
  const stream = canvas.captureStream(30);
  const blurredTrack = stream.getVideoTracks()[0];
  await replaceVideoTrack(blurredTrack);
};

setInterval(applyBlur, 33); // 30 fps
```
* Computationally expensive → May impact low-end devices
* Show performance warning if CPU > 80%
EC49. Virtual background during video call
* User selects virtual background image
* Similar to background blur but replaces instead of blurs
* Preview before applying
* Library of pre-made backgrounds
* Option to upload custom background
* Show disclaimer: "May not work perfectly in low light"
EC50. Call forwarding (forward to another user)
* During call, user wants to transfer to colleague
* Click "Transfer Call" button
* Select user to transfer to
* Options:
  * "Warm transfer" (announce first)
  * "Cold transfer" (direct transfer)
* Original caller stays connected during warm transfer
* After confirmation: Original user leaves, new user joins
EC51. Call waiting (second call while on first)
* User receives second call while already in call
* Show notification with options:
  * "Hold current call and answer"
  * "Decline"
  * "Send to voicemail" (if enabled)
* If "Hold": First call paused, second call answered
* Can switch between calls or merge (3-way call)
EC52. International calling (different time zones)
* System detects participant time zones
* Shows local time for each participant in call info
* Calendar integration accounts for time zones
* Call history displays times in user's local time zone

## Accessibility Requirements

### Keyboard Navigation
* Tab/Shift+Tab to navigate between call controls
* Enter/Space to activate buttons
* Escape to close modals/settings
* Keyboard shortcuts for common actions:
  * M - Toggle mute
  * V - Toggle video
  * S - Toggle screen share
  * C - Open chat
  * E - End call
  * +/- - Adjust volume
  * F - Toggle fullscreen
  * Space - Push to talk (hold)

### Screen Reader Support
* Call status announced: "Call initiated with Sarah Johnson"
* Connection state changes announced: "Call connected", "Reconnecting...", "Call ended"
* Participant events announced:
  * "Michael Chen joined the call"
  * "Sarah Johnson left the call"
  * "David Park's microphone is muted"
* Control states announced:
  * "Microphone muted"
  * "Camera off"
  * "Screen sharing active"
* Quality changes announced: "Connection quality: Poor. Consider switching to audio only."
* Recording status: "Call recording started. All participants have consented."
* Incoming call announced with full context: "Incoming video call from John Doe. Answer, decline, or ignore."

### Visual Accessibility
* Minimum contrast ratio 4.5:1 for all text and controls
* Call quality indicators use both color and text:
  * 🟢 "Excellent" (not just green dot)
  * 🟡 "Good"
  * 🔴 "Poor"
* Focus indicators visible with 2px outline
* Mute status uses icon + text: 🔇 "Muted"
* Video off shows icon + text: 📹❌ "Camera Off"
* High contrast mode support
* No color-only information (always include icon/text)

### Mobile Accessibility
* Touch targets minimum 44x44pt (iOS) / 48x48dp (Android)
* VoiceOver/TalkBack full support
* Dynamic Type support for text scaling
* Haptic feedback on important actions:
  * Call answered (success haptic)
  * Call ended (impact haptic)
  * Mute toggled (selection haptic)
* Reduce Motion respected (no animated transitions if disabled)
* Large buttons for critical actions (Answer, Decline, End)
Essam
**Audio Accessibility:**
- Visual indicators for audio events (for deaf/hard of hearing users):  
  - Incoming call: Visual notification + banner (no sound dependency)  
  - Speaking indicators: Green ring around participant avatar  
  - Mute status: Clear visual indicator  
  - Call quality issues: Text warnings, not just audio alerts  
- Captions/Transcription (future feature):  
  - Live captions during call  
  - Saved transcript with recording  
- Volume controls with visual feedback  

---

#### Performance Targets

**Web Application:**
- Call initiation (button click to ringing): <1 second  
- Call acceptance (accept to video rendering): <2 seconds  
- WebRTC connection establishment: <3 seconds (P95)  
- ICE gathering: <1.5 seconds  
- SDP exchange (offer/answer): <500ms  
- First video frame displayed: <2 seconds from connection  
- Screen share start: <1 second  
- Device settings change (mic/camera switch): <500ms  
- In-call chat message send: <300ms  
- Call controls response (mute/video toggle): <100ms  
- End call (disconnect all): <500ms  
- Call history page load: <1 second  
- Recordings page load: <1.2 seconds  
- Recording playback start: <2 seconds  

**Mobile Application:**
- Incoming call notification display: <500ms  
- Call UI render (incoming): <800ms  
- Call acceptance to connection: <2.5 seconds  
- Camera switch: <400ms  
- Speaker/earpiece toggle: <200ms  
- Call controls response: <150ms  
- Background to foreground transition: <500ms  
- PiP mode activation: <300ms  
- Call history screen render: <800ms  
- Recording thumbnail load: <600ms per item  

**Backend Performance:**
- Create call session: <200ms (P95)  
- Accept/reject call: <150ms (P95)  
- End call: <100ms (P95)  
- ICE candidate relay: <30ms (P95)  
- SDP offer/answer relay: <50ms (P95)  
- Add participant: <200ms (P95)  
- Start/stop recording: <300ms (P95)  
- Submit quality metrics: <100ms (P95)  
- Get call history: <250ms (P95)  
- Get call details: <150ms (P95)  
- Mark call as missed: <100ms (P95)  

**WebRTC Performance:**
- Target latency (RTT): <100ms (excellent), <200ms (good)  
- Target packet loss: <1% (excellent), <3% (acceptable)  
- Target jitter: <30ms  
- Video encoding latency: <50ms  
- Audio encoding latency: <20ms  
- Video frame rate: 30fps (HD), 24fps (SD), 15fps (LD)  
- Audio sample rate: 48kHz (Opus codec)  

**Network Requirements:**
- Minimum bandwidth (audio only): 100 kbps (bidirectional)  
- Recommended bandwidth (audio only): 150 kbps  
- Minimum bandwidth (video 360p): 500 kbps (bidirectional)  
- Recommended bandwidth (video 720p): 2.5 Mbps  
- Recommended bandwidth (video 1080p): 5 Mbps  
- Screen share bandwidth: 1-3 Mbps (depending on content)  

**Resource Usage:**
- CPU usage (video call): <40% (target), <60% (acceptable)  
- CPU usage (audio call): <15%  
- CPU usage (screen share): <50%  
- Memory usage (active call): <300 MB (web), <150 MB (mobile)  
- Battery drain (mobile, video call): <15% per 30 minutes  
- Battery drain (mobile, audio call): <5% per 30 minutes  

**Database Queries:**
- Lookup call by ID: <30ms (indexed on call.id)  
- Get user call history: <100ms (indexed on user_id, created_at DESC)  
- Get missed calls: <80ms (indexed on status, created_at)  
- Get active calls: <50ms (indexed on status, created_at)  
- Recording metadata lookup: <40ms (indexed on call_id)  
- Call quality metrics insert: <50ms  
- Participant lookup: <30ms (indexed on call_id, user_id)  

**Caching Strategy:**
- Call history cached for 2 minutes  
- User presence cached for 30 seconds  
- Device preferences cached for 10 minutes  
- ICE server configuration cached for 1 hour  
- Recording URLs cached for 10 minutes (signed URLs)  
- Quality metrics aggregated every 10 seconds, cached for 1 minute  
- Cache invalidation on call end, recording upload, settings change  

---

#### Security Measures

**Authentication & Authorization:**
- All call API endpoints require valid JWT token  
- Call participants verified via conversation membership  
- Call ID includes cryptographically secure random token (128-bit entropy)  
- Only call participants can access call details  
- Recording access restricted to call participants only  
- Admin override for moderation purposes (logged)  
- Token rotation every 15 minutes during active call  

**WebRTC Security:**
- Mandatory encryption (DTLS-SRTP)  
- Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) for key exchange  
- ICE consent freshness checks (every 30 seconds)  
- TURN credentials short-lived (5-minute expiry)  
- STUN/TURN servers authenticated via username/password  
- No unencrypted media transmission (enforce encrypted transports)  
- Certificate pinning for signaling WebSocket connection  
- SDP sanitization (prevent injection attacks)  

**Signaling Security:**
- WebSocket connection requires authentication token  
- TLS 1.3 for all signaling traffic  
- Message signing (HMAC-SHA256)  
- Replay attack protection (message nonces)  
- Rate limiting on signaling messages:  
  - ICE candidates: 100 per minute  
  - SDP offers: 10 per minute  
  - Connection attempts: 20 per hour  
- Origin validation for WebSocket connections  
- Disconnect stale connections after 30 seconds of inactivity  

**Recording Security:**
- Recording requires explicit consent from all participants (GDPR compliance)  
- Consent logged with timestamp and participant IDs  
- Recordings encrypted at rest (AES-256)  
- Recording files stored in separate storage bucket (access controlled)  
- Download URLs signed with 1-hour expiry  
- Recording deletion is permanent (no recovery)  
- Recording metadata encrypted (participant names, timestamps)  
- Recording transcriptions (future) anonymized for analysis  

**Privacy Protection:**
- Call metadata (duration, quality) stored separately from conversation content  
- PII in quality metrics hashed before analytics  
- Screen share requires explicit permission (OS-level)  
- No recording of screen share without consent  
- Participant IP addresses not exposed to other participants  
- Call participant list only visible to participants  
- Missed call notifications don't reveal caller's location/IP  
- Call history can be deleted by user (GDPR right to erasure)  

**Rate Limiting:**
- Call initiation: 20 per hour per user (prevents abuse)  
- Call acceptance: 50 per hour (prevents spam)  
- ICE candidate submission: 100 per call per user  
- Quality metrics submission: 120 per hour per call (one every 30s)  
- Recording start: 10 per day per user  
- Call history queries: 100 per hour per user  
- Signaling messages: 500 per minute per connection  

**Abuse Prevention:**
- Automatic call termination if reported by participant  
- Max call duration: 8 hours (prevents zombie connections)  
- Max recording size: 2 GB per call  
- Suspicious patterns flagged:  
  - Multiple declined calls (spam detection)  
  - Abnormal call frequency (>50 calls/day)  
  - Rapid call initiations (>5 calls/minute)  
- Temporary call ban for abusive behavior (24-48 hours)  
- Admin can disable call permissions per user  

**Audit Logging:**
- All call CRUD operations logged with user_id, IP, timestamp  
- Call consent events logged (recording, screen share)  
- Permission changes logged (microphone, camera grants/denies)  
- Failed call attempts logged (for security analysis)  
- Unusual patterns logged (e.g., calls at 3 AM)  
- Admin actions on calls logged (force-end, delete recording)  
- Logs retained for 1 year, then archived  
- Audit logs encrypted and access-controlled  

**Compliance:**
- GDPR-compliant data handling (consent, deletion, portability)  
- HIPAA-ready (if healthcare clients): encrypted recordings, audit trails  
- COPPA-compliant (no calls for users <13 without parental consent)  
- CCPA-compliant (California residents can request call data deletion)  
- EU data residency (calls routed through EU TURN servers if needed)  
- Recording retention policies configurable per tenant
